Croatia.best_time_note: May-June and September give warm sea, open ferries and half the crowds of July-August, when the coast is packed and prices peak.

rail.note: Trains only really work Zagreb-Rijeka/Osijek; there is NO rail south of Split, so along the Dalmatian coast buses and ferries beat trains every time.

bus.note: Buses are the backbone of coastal travel; compare and book on GetByBus or FlixBus, and pay the ~1 EUR luggage fee in cash to the driver.

driving.tolls: Ticket-based motorway tolls (Zagreb-Split ~25-28 EUR); through 2026 you still pay at booths, before the Crolibertas free-flow camera system replaces them (planned late 2026/March 2027).
warnings: Bura wind can close the A1 and Krk/Pag bridges to vans and campers
Since the Pelješac Bridge you can drive Split-Dubrovnik without crossing Bosnia at Neum
Rental cross-border approval needed for BiH/Montenegro/Serbia; many agencies exclude Kosovo
August border queues at BiH/Montenegro/Serbia crossings (Schengen external border) can exceed 2 hours
driving.car_recommended_for: Istria hill towns (Motovun, Grožnjan), Plitvice+Krka combos, Pag and Cres back roads
driving.car_not_needed_in: Dubrovnik, Split, Hvar and other car-free old towns and islands, ferries and buses cover them

must_see.name: Dubrovnik Old Town
must_see.why: Walk the intact medieval walls at 8am or after 5pm to dodge cruise-ship waves.

must_see.name: Plitvice Lakes
must_see.why: Sixteen terraced lakes linked by waterfalls; book timed entry online in summer.

must_see.name: Diocletian's Palace, Split
must_see.why: A living Roman palace where 3,000 people still reside inside the ancient walls.

must_see.name: Rovinj
must_see.why: Venetian fishing town that is prettier and cheaper than Dubrovnik with a fraction of the crowds.

must_see.name: Motovun & Grožnjan
must_see.why: Truffle-rich hill towns above the Mirna valley, best strung together by car.

must_see.name: Kornati archipelago
must_see.why: 89 stark, near-uninhabited islands best seen on a day sail from Murter or Zadar.

must_see.name: Zadar sea organ
must_see.why: Waves play an actual organ at sunset, Hitchcock called this the world's best sunset.

must_see.name: Stiniva cove, Vis
must_see.why: A pebble cove behind a rock gate on Croatia's most remote major island.

must_see.name: Rastoke
must_see.why: Watermill hamlet built over waterfalls, a mini-Plitvice most tourists drive past.

must_see.name: Lubenice, Cres
must_see.why: 4,000-year-old cliff village above one of the Adriatic's most beautiful hidden beaches.

must_see.name: Krka National Park
must_see.why: Waterfall cascades near Šibenik; go early, swimming below Skradinski Buk is now banned.

insights: Croatia has used the euro and been in Schengen since 1 January 2023, no exchange or passport checks coming from the EU.
Wear beach shoes: sea urchins are everywhere on rocky Adriatic beaches, and most beaches are pebble, not sand.
Dubrovnik gets 2-4 cruise ships a day in season; check the cruise calendar and visit walls before 9am.
Tap water is safe to drink everywhere, including islands.
Card acceptance is near-universal, but small konoba taverns and market stalls may still want cash.
Ferries (Jadrolinija, Krilo) sell out in August, book island catamarans a few days ahead.
Sobe (private rooms) are often better value than hotels; look for blue 'sobe/apartments' signs or Booking.
Avoid Euronet ATMs and always choose to be charged in EUR, never with dynamic currency conversion.

Slovenia.best_time_note: Late May-June and September have green valleys, hikeable Alps and no Bled crowds; July-August is busy and afternoon storms hit the mountains.

rail.note: Rail is decent by Balkan standards: cheap and scenic Ljubljana-Lesce-Bled and the Bohinj line, but for the Soča valley and Logar valley you need bus or car.

bus.note: Buses reach Bled, Bohinj and Bovec better than trains; in July-August a direct Ljubljana-Bovec service crosses the spectacular Vršič pass.

driving.vignette: E-vignette required on motorways: 16 EUR/7 days, 32 EUR/month, 117.50 EUR/year for cars (2026); buy at evinjeta.dars.si, it is plate-linked, camera-enforced, fines 300+ EUR.
driving.tolls: Vignette covers motorways; the Karavanke tunnel to Austria costs extra (~8 EUR). From 1 Jan 2026 the coastal H5/H6 expressways near Koper are vignette-free.
warnings: Vršič pass (50 hairpins) is often closed by snow October-May
ANPR cameras catch missing e-vignettes within minutes of entering a motorway
You can skip the vignette entirely by using parallel regional roads, which are slow but scenic
driving.car_recommended_for: Soča valley, Logar valley, Goriška Brda wine hills and linking Julian Alps trailheads
driving.car_not_needed_in: Ljubljana, Bled and Piran, trains/buses connect them and old towns are pedestrianised

must_see.name: Lake Bled
must_see.why: The island church and clifftop castle are iconic; row yourself out or walk the 6 km shore loop before 9am.

must_see.name: Lake Bohinj
must_see.why: Bigger, wilder and far quieter than Bled, 25 minutes further up the valley.

must_see.name: Ljubljana old town
must_see.why: Car-free riverside capital of dragon bridges and Plečnik architecture, walkable in a day.

must_see.name: Soča valley (Bovec/Kobarid)
must_see.why: An unreal emerald river with rafting, WWI history and the Tolmin gorges.

must_see.name: Vintgar gorge
must_see.why: Boardwalks hang over turquoise rapids 4 km from Bled; timed tickets in summer.

must_see.name: Piran
must_see.why: Venetian salt town on a tiny peninsula, Slovenia's 47 km of coast at its best.

must_see.name: Škocjan Caves
must_see.why: UNESCO cave with a 146 m underground canyon, less commercial than Postojna.

must_see.name: Velika Planina
must_see.why: Herders' plateau of shingled huts reached by cable car, buy cheese from the shepherds.

must_see.name: Logar valley (Logarska dolina)
must_see.why: A glacial dead-end valley locals rank above Bled and tourists rarely find.

must_see.name: Predjama Castle
must_see.why: Renaissance castle built into a cave mouth, easily paired with Postojna Cave.

must_see.name: Goriška Brda
must_see.why: Slovenia's Tuscany: orange wine, cherries and hill villages on the Italian border.

insights: Slovenia is compact, nowhere is more than 2.5 hours' drive from Ljubljana, so one base can cover a lot.
Buy the e-vignette online before touching any motorway, including the short stretch from the Austrian or Croatian border.
Tap water is excellent everywhere; Ljubljana has free public drinking fountains.
Cards are accepted almost everywhere, but mountain huts and some Bled cream-cake kiosks are cash-only.
Mountain weather turns fast: afternoon thunderstorms are routine in July-August, so start hikes early.
Bled in August is shoulder-to-shoulder; sleep in Bohinj or Radovljica instead and day-trip in.
Slovenia is one of Europe's safest countries; the main tourist 'hazard' is underestimating hiking trails graded as easy.

Bosnia and Herzegovina.best_time_note: May-June and September are warm without Herzegovina's brutal 40°C July heat; Sarajevo is also lovely under snow if you come for cheap skiing.

rail.note: Rail is minimal, but the twice-daily Sarajevo-Mostar train (~6 EUR) through the Neretva canyon is one of Europe's most scenic rides, take it one way, bus the other.

bus.note: Buses are the backbone; check GetByBus or BalkanViator but buy at the station, pay the ~1 KM token to enter platforms and small bag fees in cash.

driving.tolls: Cheap booth tolls on the short A1 motorway sections (Sarajevo-Zenica/ Mostar direction); pay cash in KM or card. Most of the country is toll-free single-carriageway.
warnings: Roads are winding two-lane mountain routes, average 50-60 km/h, not Google's estimates
Never wander off marked paths in rural areas: residual landmines from the 1990s remain in remote hills
Winter tyres mandatory 1 Nov-15 Apr; fog and ice in Sarajevo's valleys
Most EU green cards now cover BiH, but confirm the BIH box on yours before crossing; rentals need cross-border approval
driving.car_recommended_for: Una National Park, Lukomir, Sutjeska/Maglić and stringing Herzegovina's Kravice-Počitelj-Blagaj loop
driving.car_not_needed_in: Sarajevo and Mostar, both compact, linked by scenic train, with day tours covering Herzegovina highlights

must_see.name: Baščaršija, Sarajevo
must_see.why: Ottoman bazaar where you drink Bosnian coffee metres from Austro-Hungarian boulevards, Europe's east-west seam.

must_see.name: Stari Most, Mostar
must_see.why: The rebuilt 16th-century bridge with local divers leaping 24 m; stay overnight for the after-daytrippers calm.

must_see.name: Blagaj Tekke
must_see.why: A dervish monastery pressed against a cliff where the Buna river erupts from a cave.

must_see.name: Kravice waterfalls
must_see.why: A 120 m arc of falls you can swim beneath, a mini Niagara with beach bars.

must_see.name: Počitelj
must_see.why: Crumbling Ottoman fortress village of fig sellers and pomegranate juice above the Neretva.

must_see.name: Lukomir
must_see.why: Bosnia's highest, most remote village, medieval stećci tombstones and shepherds at 1,469 m.

must_see.name: Una National Park
must_see.why: Plitvice-style travertine falls at Štrbački Buk and Martin Brod without the crowds or price.

must_see.name: Jajce
must_see.why: A 20 m waterfall in the town centre plus the medieval fortress and Pliva watermills.

must_see.name: Sutjeska NP & Maglić
must_see.why: The Perućica primeval forest and Bosnia's highest peak in its oldest national park.

must_see.name: Trebinje
must_see.why: Wine-country town 30 min from Dubrovnik at half the price, with the Arslanagić bridge.

must_see.name: Travnik
must_see.why: Ottoman vizier capital famous for its fortress, Ivo Andrić and Bosnia's best ćevapi rivalry.

insights: The convertible mark (BAM/KM) is pegged at 1.95583 to the euro; euros are often accepted in Mostar and tourist spots at ~2 KM = 1 EUR, but change is given in KM.
This is a cash country: many guesthouses, ćevabdžinice and buses are cash-only, so withdraw KM from bank ATMs (avoid Euronet).
Tap water is safe in Sarajevo, Mostar and most towns, Bosnians proudly drink from public fountains.
Coffee is a ritual: Bosnian kafa comes in a džezva with rahat lokum, and rushing it is missing the point.
Stray dogs are common; they are mostly docile, but give packs space at night.
Do not photograph the ruined buildings' interiors or stray off paths in the countryside, unexploded mines persist in remote areas.
Mostar empties beautifully after 17:00 when Dubrovnik day-trip buses leave, stay the night.
August queues at the Croatian border (EU external) can be long; cross early morning.

Montenegro.best_time_note: June and September combine swimmable sea with open Durmitor trails; in August the tiny coast absorbs regional holiday traffic and prices double.

rail.note: Only two lines matter: the spectacular Bar-Podgorica-Belgrade route (254 tunnels, Mala Rijeka viaduct) is a must-ride, but for the coast and mountains buses win.

bus.note: Frequent coastal buses (Herceg Novi-Kotor-Budva-Bar) are the backbone; book on busticket4.me or pay cash at stations, plus ~1 EUR per bag to the driver.

driving.tolls: Sozina tunnel (Podgorica-Bar) ~2.50 EUR per direction; the new Bar-Mateševo motorway section is tolled. Everything else is toll-free but slow.
warnings: Kotor-Lovćen serpentine (25 hairpins) and Durmitor's P14 are narrow with sheer drops, confident drivers only
Coastal Jadranska magistrala crawls in August; expect hours for 50 km
Rentals from Montenegro usually may not enter Kosovo and need written approval for other borders
Police radar checks are frequent; fines are collected on the spot
driving.car_recommended_for: Durmitor ring road, Lovćen, Lake Skadar villages and the Prokletije, the mountains are the point
driving.car_not_needed_in: The Kotor-Budva coast, where buses run every 30-60 minutes and old towns are car-free

must_see.name: Kotor old town & walls
must_see.why: Climb the 1,350 steps to St John's fortress at dawn, before cruise passengers land.

must_see.name: Perast & Our Lady of the Rocks
must_see.why: A one-street baroque town with a man-made island church a 5 EUR boat hop away.

must_see.name: Durmitor NP & Tara canyon
must_see.why: Europe's deepest canyon (1,300 m) plus the Black Lake and 2,500 m peaks around Žabljak.

must_see.name: Lovćen & Njegoš mausoleum
must_see.why: 461 steps to a mountaintop tomb with the whole country spread below.

must_see.name: Ostrog Monastery
must_see.why: A white monastery fused into a vertical cliff face, the Balkans' most striking pilgrimage site.

must_see.name: Rijeka Crnojevića
must_see.why: The famous horseshoe river bend, sleepy fishing village and boat trips into pelican wetlands.

must_see.name: Sveti Stefan viewpoint
must_see.why: The fortified islet-turned-resort is closed to visitors, but the roadside view is free and iconic.

must_see.name: Prokletije NP
must_see.why: The 'Accursed Mountains', the wildest hiking in Europe on the Peaks of the Balkans trail.

must_see.name: Biogradska Gora
must_see.why: One of Europe's last primeval forests wrapped around a glacial lake.

must_see.name: Ulcinj & Velika Plaža
must_see.why: 12 km of sand, kitesurfing and an Ottoman-Albanian old town unlike anywhere else on this coast.

must_see.name: Cetinje
must_see.why: Faded embassies and royal museums of the old kingdom, en route to Lovćen.

insights: Montenegro uses the euro unilaterally, it is not in the eurozone or EU, so no special currency needed but expect cash-first habits.
Carry cash outside big towns; konobas, market stalls and bus drivers often refuse cards, and ATM fees vary wildly (skip Euronet).
Tap water is safe in most of the country; on the southern coast in peak summer some prefer bottled during shortages.
Kotor receives cruise ships most summer mornings; do the walls before 8am or after 17:00.
Sea urchins live on the rocky beaches around Kotor and Budva, pack water shoes.
August border queues from Croatia (Karasovići/Debeli Brijeg) regularly hit 1-2 hours; cross before 8am.
The Bar-Belgrade train is a top-5 European rail journey and costs about 24 EUR, sit on the left leaving Bar.
A 1 EUR/night tourist tax applies; unregistered stays can cause exit-fine hassles, so ensure your host registers you.

Serbia.best_time_note: May-June and September are ideal for Belgrade's outdoor kafanas and the western mountains; July brings EXIT festival and river-island beach season.

rail.note: Mostly slow, but the 200 km/h Soko train (Belgrade-Novi Sad-Subotica) is modern and cheap; for Uvac, Tara and southern Serbia buses or a car are the only real option.

bus.note: Dense intercity bus network is the workhorse; buy at stations (small platform-entry and luggage fees in cash) or check BalkanViator/polazak.rs for times.

driving.tolls: Distance-based motorway tolls paid at booths (Belgrade-Niš ~12 EUR); cash in dinars, euros accepted at poor rates, cards OK.
warnings: Cars with Serbian rental plates are generally barred from entering Kosovo, plan around it
Aggressive overtaking on single-carriageway roads; drive defensively
August weekends jam the Hungarian and Croatian border crossings with diaspora traffic
Winter tyres mandatory Nov-Apr in winter conditions
driving.car_recommended_for: Uvac canyon, Tara NP, Zlatibor, Đavolja Varoš and monastery-hopping in the southwest
driving.car_not_needed_in: Belgrade and Novi Sad, walkable centres, cheap taxis, and the Soko train links them in 36 minutes

must_see.name: Belgrade Kalemegdan & Skadarlija
must_see.why: Fortress sunsets over the Sava-Danube confluence, then live music in the bohemian quarter.

must_see.name: Novi Sad & Petrovaradin
must_see.why: Habsburg-flavoured city under the 'Gibraltar of the Danube', home of EXIT festival.

must_see.name: Uvac canyon meanders
must_see.why: Emerald river switchbacks patrolled by griffon vultures, Serbia's most jaw-dropping viewpoint.

must_see.name: Tara National Park
must_see.why: Banjska Stena viewpoint over the Drina canyon and the famous tiny Drina river house.

must_see.name: Drvengrad & Šargan Eight
must_see.why: Kusturica's wooden ethno-village plus a figure-eight heritage railway through the mountains.

must_see.name: Studenica Monastery
must_see.why: UNESCO 12th-century monastery with white marble churches and Byzantine frescoes.

must_see.name: Đavolja Varoš
must_see.why: 202 eerie earth pyramids ('Devil's Town') formed by erosion, genuinely otherworldly.

must_see.name: Golubac Fortress & Iron Gates
must_see.why: A 10-tower fortress rising straight from the Danube at the gateway to Europe's mightiest gorge.

must_see.name: Niš
must_see.why: Constantine's birthplace with the chilling Skull Tower and Serbia's best grilled-meat culture.

must_see.name: Subotica
must_see.why: Hungarian-Serbian art nouveau fantasy architecture near Palić lake.

must_see.name: Sremski Karlovci
must_see.why: Baroque wine town, taste bermet, the dessert wine allegedly served on the Titanic.

insights: Pay in dinars (RSD, ~117 = 1 EUR); euros are widely quoted for apartments but street exchange offices (menjačnica) beat airport and ATM rates.
Skip Euronet ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion, fees can reach 8 percent.
Tap water is safe in Belgrade and most cities; in Vojvodina villages locals often prefer bottled.
Kafana culture is the real attraction: expect live tamburaši music, rakija toasts and smoking indoors more than you're used to.
If you plan Kosovo AND Serbia overland, enter Kosovo FROM Serbia first (or transit a third country), see the Kosovo entry.
Belgrade's splavovi (river barge clubs) run all night in summer; take licensed taxis (Pink, Lux) or CarGo, never street cabs at the station.
Stray dogs are common but usually harmless; rabies risk is negligible in cities.
Intercity buses charge ~100 RSD per suitcase in cash and stations charge a small platform fee (peronska karta).

Kosovo.best_time_note: May-June and September are green and mild for Rugova and Sharr hiking; August adds diaspora crowds and Dokufest buzz, while winter means cheap skiing at Brezovica.

rail.note: Rail is near-irrelevant: one slow Pristina-Peja line runs daily. Take buses, they are cheap, frequent and always faster.

bus.note: Buses are the backbone: Pristina-Prizren ~4 EUR, Pristina-Peja ~4 EUR, roughly hourly; pay the driver in cash, check BalkanViator or the station board for times.

driving.tolls: No tolls; the excellent R7 motorway to Albania (Rruga e Kombit) is free on the Kosovo side.
warnings: EU green cards do NOT cover Kosovo, buy border third-party insurance (~30 EUR/15 days) unless your policy lists XK
Rentals from Serbia may not enter Kosovo, and most Kosovo rentals may not enter Serbia
Roads are good on main axes but village roads and driving discipline are rough
Avoid political discussions at the northern (Serb-majority) crossings and follow local advice in North Mitrovica
driving.car_recommended_for: Rugova canyon, Mirusha waterfalls, Brezovica and monastery-hopping, public transport misses all of them
driving.car_not_needed_in: Pristina and Prizren, both compact and connected by frequent cheap buses

must_see.name: Prizren old town
must_see.why: Kosovo's prettiest city: Ottoman bridge, league house and a fortress sunset over minarets and church towers.

must_see.name: Pristina
must_see.why: The brutalist National Library, NEWBORN monument and Europe's best-value macchiato culture.

must_see.name: Rugova canyon
must_see.why: A 1,000 m-deep gorge with via ferratas and the start of the Peaks of the Balkans trail.

must_see.name: Visoki Dečani Monastery
must_see.why: UNESCO Serbian-Orthodox monastery with 1,000 m2 of frescoes, still under KFOR guard, bring your passport.

must_see.name: Gračanica Monastery
must_see.why: A 14th-century Byzantine masterpiece in a Serb enclave 20 minutes from the capital.

must_see.name: Gjakova old bazaar
must_see.why: The longest Ottoman çarshia in the Balkans, rebuilt after 1999 and refreshingly tourist-free.

must_see.name: Mirusha waterfalls
must_see.why: Thirteen terraced falls and swimming holes carved into a small canyon.

must_see.name: Brezovica & Sharr Mountains
must_see.why: Faded Yugoslav ski resort turned budget powder secret, and summer trailhead for the Sharr range.

must_see.name: Peja and its Patriarchate
must_see.why: Bazaar town beneath the Accursed Mountains with the UNESCO Patriarchate monastery at the canyon mouth.

must_see.name: Bear Sanctuary Prishtina
must_see.why: Rescued restaurant bears in a well-run sanctuary, an easy, feel-good half-day trip.

insights: Kosovo uses the euro unilaterally (not an eurozone member), and since 2024 it is the only legal tender, dinar payments were phased out except in some Serb enclaves.

CRITICAL ROUTING RULE: Serbia treats arrival via Kosovo as illegal entry; you can only cross Kosovo->Serbia if you first entered Kosovo FROM Serbia. Otherwise loop via North Macedonia, Albania or Montenegro.
A Kosovo entry stamp is not a problem for later Serbia trips via other borders, but Serbian officers may cancel it.
Cash rules: ATMs are plentiful in cities but many cafes, buses and guesthouses are cash-only.
Tap water is generally chlorinated and drinkable in Pristina, but most travellers stick to cheap bottled water.
Kosovo is one of Europe's cheapest destinations: a macchiato ~1 EUR, a full dinner 5-8 EUR.
People are famously hospitable and pro-Western; English and German are widely spoken by the young diaspora generation.
Stray dogs roam city edges at night, carry on confidently and they ignore you.

Albania.best_time_note: Late May-June and September give a warm, uncrowded Riviera and snow-free Theth trails; August is overrun by diaspora and Italian holidaymakers with doubled prices.

rail.note: Forget trains entirely, the skeletal network is slower than walking pace matters. Buses and furgon minibuses are how Albania moves.

operators: intercity buses from Tirana's North/South terminals
bus.note: Buses/furgons are cheap (Tirana-Saranda ~13 EUR) but schedules are oral tradition; check gjirafa or ask your host, arrive early, pay the driver in lek.

driving.tolls: Only the A1 'Rruga e Kombit' toward Kosovo has a toll (~2.5-5 EUR for cars); everything else is free.
warnings: Albanian driving is assertive and lane discipline loose; expect overtaking on blind bends
Watch for potholes, unlit vehicles and livestock on rural roads after dark
The Llogara tunnel (opened 2024) bypasses the pass, but the old SH8 viewpoint road is worth it in daylight
SH75 to Theth is now paved, but Valbona-Theth remains hike-only; check your rental's gravel-road clause
driving.car_recommended_for: The Albanian Riviera coves (Gjipe, Krorëz), Theth, and inland UNESCO towns, buses exist but eat whole days
driving.car_not_needed_in: Tirana (chaotic parking) and the Ksamil-Saranda strip, where local buses and taxis suffice

must_see.name: Theth & the Blue Eye of Theth
must_see.why: Stone towers, a shingled church and a glowing spring pool at the heart of the Accursed Mountains.

must_see.name: Valbona-Theth hike
must_see.why: The Balkans' most famous day hike (6-8h) over the 1,795 m Valbona pass.

must_see.name: Lake Koman ferry
must_see.why: A 2.5-hour boat through fjord-like canyons, often called Europe's most beautiful ferry ride.

must_see.name: Berat
must_see.why: UNESCO 'town of a thousand windows' with an inhabited hilltop castle quarter.

must_see.name: Gjirokastër
must_see.why: Ottoman stone town of steep bazaars, a vast castle and Cold War tunnels.

must_see.name: Albanian Riviera (Dhërmi, Himarë, Gjipe)
must_see.why: Turquoise coves under the Ceraunian mountains; Gjipe beach is a 30-min canyon walk from the road.

must_see.name: Butrint
must_see.why: Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Venetian ruins layered in a lagoon national park.

must_see.name: Blue Eye (Syri i Kaltër)
must_see.why: A 50 m-deep karst spring of impossible blue between Saranda and Gjirokastër.

must_see.name: Tirana
must_see.why: Bunk'Art Cold War bunkers, the Blloku bar district and Mount Dajti cable car.

must_see.name: Shkodra & Rozafa Castle
must_see.why: Laid-back cycling city between lake and Alps, the natural base before Theth or Koman.

must_see.name: Krujë
must_see.why: Skanderbeg's citadel and an authentic Ottoman bazaar 40 minutes from Tirana airport.

must_see.name: Apollonia
must_see.why: A Greek city where Augustus studied, sitting alone in olive-grove hills with no crowds.

insights: Currency is the lek (ALL), roughly 95-100 = 1 EUR in 2026; prices are sometimes quoted in 'old lek' (add a zero), so confirm which is meant.
Cash is king outside Tirana and resort hotels, many guesthouses, furgons and beach bars are cash-only; euros often accepted at rounded-up rates.
Don't drink the tap water in most of the country; large cheap bottles are everywhere (Tirana's supply is chlorinated but locals still buy bottled).
Ryanair's Tirana base makes Albania one of the cheapest Balkan gateways from Belgian airports.
Nodding for 'no' and shaking for 'yes' persists among older Albanians, confirm verbally.
Stray dogs are common; most are harmless, but hikers in the Alps should give sheepdog-guarded flocks a wide berth.
Sea urchins live on the Riviera's rocky entries, pack water shoes for Gjipe and Himarë.
Xhiro time: whole towns promenade at dusk and cafes charge ~1 EUR for espresso; budget accordingly, it is delightfully cheap.
August ferries and Riviera rooms sell out weeks ahead; June/September need no bookings at all.
events: Tirana's Summer Day (Dita e Verës, 14 Mar)

North Macedonia.best_time_note: May-June and September are perfect for Lake Ohrid swims and Galičica hikes; Skopje bakes above 35°C in mid-summer while Ohrid peaks with regional tourists.

rail.note: Trains are few, slow and skip Ohrid entirely, treat rail as a curiosity (Skopje-Bitola exists) and take buses for everything.

operators: local operators from Skopje bus station
bus.note: Buses are the backbone: Skopje-Ohrid ~8-10 EUR in 3 hours, roughly hourly in summer; buy at the station (cash) and check BalkanViator for times.

driving.tolls: Small booth tolls on the A1/A2 motorways (1-2.5 EUR per station, cash denars or card); the whole Skopje-Ohrid drive costs a few euros.
warnings: Radar traps are frequent and speed fines collected on the spot
The Galičica summit road and Mavrovo backroads are narrow and unbarriered
Stray dogs and slow farm vehicles appear on rural highways
Green cards from EU insurers cover North Macedonia (MK box), verify before the border
driving.car_recommended_for: Galičica panoramic road, Mavrovo, Prespa lake and monastery-hopping around Bitola
driving.car_not_needed_in: Skopje and Ohrid town, both walkable with cheap taxis, linked by frequent buses

must_see.name: Ohrid old town & St. John at Kaneo
must_see.why: Byzantine churches above a 3-million-year-old UNESCO lake, the cliff-edge Kaneo church is the Balkans' postcard.

must_see.name: Ohrid backstreets & Plaošnik
must_see.why: Skip the promenade for the cobbled upper lanes, Roman theatre and Samuel's fortress at dusk.

must_see.name: St. Naum & Ohrid springs
must_see.why: A 10th-century monastery with peacocks, and boat rides over glass-clear springs near the Albanian border.

must_see.name: Matka Canyon
must_see.why: Kayak past cliff monasteries to Vrelo cave, 40 minutes from the capital.

must_see.name: Skopje old bazaar
must_see.why: The Balkans' second-largest Ottoman čaršija, a genuine antidote to the city's kitsch neoclassical makeover.

must_see.name: Galičica National Park
must_see.why: A summit road with both lakes at your feet, one of Europe's great unknown viewpoints.

must_see.name: Bitola & Heraclea Lyncestis
must_see.why: Consular-era cafe boulevard plus Roman mosaics that you'll likely have to yourself.

must_see.name: Kruševo
must_see.why: The Balkans' highest town: revolutionary history, the Makedonium monument and paragliding.

must_see.name: Mavrovo & Jovan Bigorski
must_see.why: Ski-and-hike national park with a spectacular fresco-filled monastery on the Radika gorge road.

must_see.name: Painted Mosque, Tetovo
must_see.why: A 15th-century mosque wrapped in 30,000 hand-painted floral panels.

must_see.name: Stobi
must_see.why: Roman provincial capital ruins conveniently beside the A1 motorway and Tikveš wine country.

insights: Pay in denars (MKD, ~61.5 = 1 EUR, stable peg); exchange offices in Skopje's bazaar give near mid-market rates and many guesthouses quote euros.
Cash first: cards work in supermarkets and hotels, but bazaar stalls, buses, taxis and many kafanas want denars.
Tap water is safe in Skopje, Ohrid and Bitola, among the best in the Balkans.
Ohrid trout is endangered and its fishing restricted; the 'Ohrid trout' on menus is usually farmed, consider lake alternatives like belvica.
August packs Ohrid with regional tourists; June and September have 25°C water without the crowds.
Skopje's centre is a surreal open-air lesson in nation-branding (Skopje 2014 project), enjoy it, then cross the Stone Bridge to the real Ottoman city.
Stray dogs are common in Skopje; they wear ear tags and are generally placid.
Wine is a bargain: Tikveš region tastings (Vranec, Temjanika) cost a fraction of anywhere in the EU.

Poland.best_time_note: May-June and September bring warm days without July-August crowds at Kraków and the Baltic coast; winter is great for cheap Zakopane skiing.

rail.note: Book ~30 days ahead for Promo fares from ~€5; TLK/IC 2nd class is cheap, only the EIP Pendolino needs a pricier compulsory reservation.

bus.note: FlixBus dominates intercity routes with fares from €3-8; Polonus is solid for Warsaw connections.

driving.tolls: No vignette for cars; state motorways are free for cars, only private A1/A2/A4 sections (e.g. Katowice-Kraków) charge at toll gates, card or cash.
warnings: Near-zero alcohol limit (0.02%)
Headlights mandatory 24/7 year-round
Aggressive overtaking on single-carriageway DK national roads - keep right
driving.car_recommended_for: Bieszczady mountains, Masurian Lakes, Baltic coast villages (Hel, Łeba) and Podlasie/Białowieża
driving.car_not_needed_in: Kraków, Warsaw, Gdańsk and Wrocław - trains and trams cover them well

must_see.name: Kraków Old Town & Wawel
must_see.why: Best-preserved medieval market square in Europe with cheap food and nightlife in Kazimierz.

must_see.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
must_see.why: Essential, sobering memorial; book the free entry slot weeks ahead on the official site.

must_see.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
must_see.why: Underground chapels carved entirely from salt, an easy half-day from Kraków.

must_see.name: Zakopane & Tatra trails
must_see.why: Alpine hiking (Morskie Oko) at a fraction of Alps prices; buses from Kraków cost ~€5.

must_see.name: Gdańsk
must_see.why: Rebuilt Hanseatic old town, WWII history and amber shops, with Sopot beach next door.

must_see.name: Malbork Castle
must_see.why: World's largest brick castle, an easy train stop between Warsaw and Gdańsk.

must_see.name: Wrocław
must_see.why: Colourful market square, 100+ islands and bridges, and a hunt for bronze gnomes.

must_see.name: Toruń
must_see.why: Untouched Gothic old town, birthplace of Copernicus and of Poland's gingerbread.

must_see.name: Masurian Lakes
must_see.why: 2,000+ lakes for cheap sailing and kayaking, best reached by car.

must_see.name: Bieszczady Mountains
must_see.why: Genuinely wild southeast corner with open ridge meadows, wolves and almost no tourists.

must_see.name: Kazimierz Dolny
must_see.why: Artists' town on the Vistula with renaissance facades and loess gorges, skipped by foreigners.

must_see.name: Białowieża Forest
must_see.why: Europe's last primeval lowland forest and wild bison herds.

insights: Never use Euronet ATMs and always decline dynamic currency conversion - pay and withdraw in PLN, saving 5-10%.
Exchange cash at kantors in city centres, never at the airport; better yet just use cards, accepted everywhere.
Eat at a bar mleczny (milk bar): full traditional meal for €3-5.
Sunday trading ban: most shops and malls are closed most Sundays - stock up Saturday (Żabka corner shops stay open).
Careful when paying: saying 'dziękuję' (thank you) as you hand over cash means 'keep the change'.
Use Bolt/Uber instead of taxi ranks at stations and airports; rides are very cheap.
Tipping ~10% in sit-down restaurants; not expected in bars or milk bars.
PKP Promo train fares released ~30 days out sell out on Kraków-Warsaw-Gdańsk; book early.

Czechia.best_time_note: May-June and September give mild weather and thinner Prague crowds; December is lovely for Christmas markets but book beds early.

rail.note: Buy on cd.cz or regiojet.com; private RegioJet and Leo Express often undercut ČD on Prague-Brno-Ostrava with nicer seats and free coffee.

bus.note: RegioJet buses are famously good - attendants, screens, free hot drinks - and often cheaper than trains; FlixBus covers international runs.

driving.vignette: E-vignette required on motorways: CZK 300 (~€12)/10 days, CZK 480/30 days; buy only at official edalnice.gov.cz (electric cars exempt). Verified 2026 price list.
driving.tolls: No extra tolls for cars beyond the e-vignette.
warnings: Zero-tolerance alcohol limit (0.0%)
Headlights mandatory 24/7
Unofficial vignette resellers charge big markups - use the .gov.cz site
driving.car_recommended_for: Bohemian Switzerland, Moravian wine country, Adršpach rocks and castle-hopping in the countryside
driving.car_not_needed_in: Prague, Brno, Olomouc and Český Krumlov - trains/buses reach them easily

must_see.name: Prague Old Town & Castle
must_see.why: Charles Bridge at dawn and the castle complex; go early or late to dodge the crowds.

must_see.name: Český Krumlov
must_see.why: Fairy-tale riverside town below a renaissance castle; stay overnight after day-trippers leave.

must_see.name: Kutná Hora
must_see.why: Sedlec bone chapel and a UNESCO silver-mining town, one hour by cheap train from Prague.

must_see.name: Bohemian Switzerland NP
must_see.why: Pravčická sandstone arch and gorge boat rides, doable as a Prague day trip.

must_see.name: Brno
must_see.why: Czechia's second city has great cafés, functionalist villas and student-priced nightlife.

must_see.name: Olomouc
must_see.why: Prague's baroque beauty with almost no tourists and the pungent olomoucké tvarůžky cheese.

must_see.name: Karlovy Vary
must_see.why: Grand spa colonnades where you sip hot springs from porcelain cups.

must_see.name: Adršpach-Teplice Rocks
must_see.why: Surreal sandstone rock city with narrow gorges, popular with Polish visitors but few Westerners.

must_see.name: Mikulov & Pálava
must_see.why: Wine cellars, white cliffs and vineyard cycling near the Austrian border.

must_see.name: Telč
must_see.why: One perfect renaissance square of pastel gables, a UNESCO gem most itineraries miss.

must_see.name: Moravian Karst
must_see.why: Punkva caves with an underground river cruise and the Macocha abyss.

insights: Prague street exchange offices advertising '0% commission' use terrible rates - check the actual rate or just use a fee-free card in CZK.
Skip Euronet ATMs and always choose to be charged in CZK, never EUR (DCC).
Never hail taxis on the street in Prague - use Bolt, Uber or Liftago.
Beer (~CZK 45-60, €2-2.5) is cheaper than bottled water; Pilsner tastes best 'z tanku' (tank-fresh).
Weekday 'polední menu' lunch specials give a soup + main for €6-8 even in Prague.
Tip by rounding up ~5-10%; tell the server the total as you pay rather than leaving coins.
Validate public transport tickets when boarding - plain-clothes inspectors fine tourists on the spot.
Czechia uses the koruna (CZK), not the euro; some tourist places take EUR at poor rates.

Slovakia.best_time_note: June-September for High Tatras hiking (many ridge trails only open 16 June-31 Oct); September adds wine-harvest festivals and empty trails.

rail.note: Very cheap; book IC Bratislava-Košice online for the best fares, and use the scenic electric TEŽ mountain railway between Tatra resorts.

bus.note: RegioJet's high-quality coaches (screens, free coffee) link Bratislava with Prague, Vienna and Košice, often for under €15.

driving.vignette: E-vignette on motorways: €10.80/10 days, €17.10/30 days; buy at official eznamka.sk (verified 2026). Also a 1-day option for €8.10.
driving.tolls: No extra tolls for cars beyond the e-vignette; most Tatra roads are vignette-free.
warnings: Zero-tolerance alcohol limit (0.0%)
Headlights mandatory 24/7
Watch for potholes and slow trucks on non-motorway routes
driving.car_recommended_for: Spiš region castles, wooden churches around Bardejov, Slovak Paradise and Orava
driving.car_not_needed_in: Bratislava, Košice and the High Tatras corridor (train to Poprad + TEŽ mountain railway)

must_see.name: High Tatras
must_see.why: Alpine peaks, lakes like Štrbské Pleso and cheap mountain huts - the Alps at half price.

must_see.name: Spiš Castle & Levoča
must_see.why: One of Europe's largest castle ruins beside a walled renaissance town, both UNESCO and uncrowded.

must_see.name: Slovenský raj (Slovak Paradise)
must_see.why: Canyon hikes on ladders and chains above waterfalls - a unique, cheap adventure day.

must_see.name: Bratislava Old Town
must_see.why: Compact, cheap capital an hour from Vienna, with castle views over the Danube.

must_see.name: Banská Štiavnica
must_see.why: Gorgeous UNESCO mining town in a volcanic caldera, beloved by Slovaks, unknown abroad.

must_see.name: Košice
must_see.why: Slovakia's second city has the country's grandest cathedral and a lively, cheap main street.

must_see.name: Bardejov
must_see.why: Perfect medieval square plus nearby UNESCO wooden churches of the Carpathians.

must_see.name: Vlkolínec
must_see.why: Living open-air village of log houses, a UNESCO time capsule.

must_see.name: Orava Castle
must_see.why: Dramatic cliff-top castle where Nosferatu (1922) was filmed.

must_see.name: Demänovská Caves & Low Tatras
must_see.why: Spectacular ice and dripstone caves under a hiking- and ski-friendly range.

insights: Slovakia uses the euro - no exchange needed, unlike its Czech, Polish and Hungarian neighbours.
Cheapest Tatras approach: train to Poprad, then the TEŽ electric railway to Štrbské Pleso/Tatranská Lomnica for a couple of euros.
High-mountain ridge trails in the Tatras close 1 Nov-15 June for protection - check before planning summit hikes.
Mountain hut (chata) dorms cost €15-25 with hearty cheap food - book popular ones ahead in summer.
Lunch menus (denné menu) run €5-7; tipping ~10% by rounding up is standard.
Kofola, the local cola, is on tap in most pubs and cheaper than Coke.
Bratislava is an easy €5-10 bus/train hop from Vienna airport - handy Ryanair alternative routing.

Hungary.best_time_note: May-June and September are warm without the stifling August heat; thermal baths are at their most atmospheric in cold months.

rail.note: Very cheap; buy on the MÁV app/site. The national monthly pass (~€50) and county passes are absurd value if you're touring for weeks.

bus.note: FlixBus for international runs; state Volánbusz reaches villages trains skip, tickets a few euros.

driving.vignette: E-vignette (e-matrica) required on motorways: D1 10-day 6,900 HUF (~€17.5), monthly 11,170 HUF (2026 prices); buy at nemzetiutdij.hu, cheaper county vignettes exist.
driving.tolls: No toll gates for cars - enforcement is by camera against your plate, so buy the vignette before entering the motorway.
warnings: Zero-tolerance alcohol limit (0.0%)
Camera enforcement means fines reach foreign drivers via rental firms
Budapest parking zones are strictly enforced
driving.car_recommended_for: Lake Balaton's north-shore villages, Tokaj and Villány wine regions, Hortobágy puszta
driving.car_not_needed_in: Budapest (dense metro/tram network) and for Eger, Pécs or Szeged, all easy by train

must_see.name: Budapest thermal baths
must_see.why: Széchenyi and Gellért are icons, but Rudas (Ottoman dome) and morning tickets are cheaper and calmer.

must_see.name: Buda Castle & Parliament
must_see.why: The Danube panorama is UNESCO-listed - walk the Chain Bridge at night for free.

must_see.name: Eger
must_see.why: Baroque town with a castle and the Valley of the Beautiful Women wine cellars (Bull's Blood by the glass for cents).

must_see.name: Lake Balaton
must_see.why: Central Europe's 'sea'; Tihany abbey views and Badacsony vineyard hikes beat the party towns.

must_see.name: Pécs
must_see.why: Mediterranean-feeling university city with Ottoman mosques and early-Christian UNESCO tombs.

must_see.name: Tokaj
must_see.why: Cellar tastings of the world's oldest classified sweet wine cost a fraction of Bordeaux.

must_see.name: Hollókő
must_see.why: Preserved Palóc folk village, UNESCO-listed, magical at Easter.

must_see.name: Danube Bend (Szentendre, Visegrád, Esztergom)
must_see.why: Riverside citadel views and an artists' town, all on suburban transport.

must_see.name: Hortobágy National Park
must_see.why: UNESCO steppe of herdsmen, grey cattle and birdlife - Hungary at its most un-touristy.

must_see.name: Szeged
must_see.why: Sunny Art Nouveau city famous for fish soup and paprika.

insights: Hungary uses the forint (HUF), not the euro; refuse EUR pricing and DCC - paying in HUF is always cheaper.
Avoid Euronet ATMs (bad rates, high fees) - use bank ATMs like OTP or Erste and decline conversion.
Never street-hail in Budapest: use Bolt or the official yellow Főtaxi; freelance cabs overcharge badly.
Check restaurant bills - a 12-15% service charge is often already added, so don't double-tip.
Thermal bath tips: bring flip-flops and a swim cap for lap pools; weekday mornings are cheapest and quietest.
The MÁV national monthly pass (~19,000 HUF/€50) covers nearly all trains and Volánbusz buses countrywide.
Ruin bars (Szimpla Kert etc.) are cheap by Western standards but pricier than normal Budapest pubs one street away.
Sunday: many shops close; big supermarkets have restricted hours around holidays.

Estonia.best_time_note: June-August brings white nights, warm(ish) Baltic beaches and open island ferries; December's Tallinn Christmas market is the fairytale alternative.

rail.note: Modern orange trains, very cheap (Tallinn-Tartu ~€10); buy in the app or onboard, no advance booking games.

bus.note: Buses beat trains for most routes; Lux Express coaches have seat screens and free coffee, Tallinn-Riga from ~€10-15 booked early.

driving.tolls: No vignette or road tolls for cars - all public roads are free.
warnings: Headlights mandatory 24/7
Winter tyres compulsory roughly Dec-Mar
Moose and deer on rural roads at dusk
driving.car_recommended_for: Saaremaa and Hiiumaa islands (car ferries), Lahemaa NP manors and bog trails, Setomaa
driving.car_not_needed_in: Tallinn and Tartu; Bolt and buses cover the cities cheaply

must_see.name: Tallinn Old Town
must_see.why: The best-preserved medieval Hanseatic core in Northern Europe, walkable in a day.

must_see.name: Lahemaa National Park
must_see.why: Bog boardwalks, boulder beaches and tsarist-era manors an hour from Tallinn.

must_see.name: Saaremaa
must_see.why: Windmills, a meteorite crater at Kaali and spa hotels - Estonia's slow-life island.

must_see.name: Tartu
must_see.why: Student capital with a leafy old town and great museums (ERM), calmer and cheaper than Tallinn.

must_see.name: Soomaa National Park
must_see.why: Canoe the 'fifth season' floods or walk peat bogs in wilderness few tourists see.

must_see.name: Pärnu
must_see.why: Estonia's summer beach capital with wooden villas and long sandy shallows.

must_see.name: Hiiumaa
must_see.why: Quieter than Saaremaa, with lighthouses and an offbeat islander humour.

must_see.name: Narva
must_see.why: EU-Russia border castle staring down Ivangorod fortress across the river - striking and cheap.

must_see.name: Setomaa
must_see.why: Distinct Seto culture with polyphonic singing and onion-domed chapels on the Russian borderlands.

must_see.name: Viljandi
must_see.why: Lakeside castle ruins and Estonia's biggest folk-music festival each July.

insights: Estonia is nearly cashless - cards and phones work everywhere, and Bolt (an Estonian company) is the cheap way around town.
Tallinn's free public transport applies to registered residents only - visitors buy a QR ticket or validate a Ühiskaart.
Old Town restaurants charge double the prices found in Telliskivi or Kalamaja - eat one street beyond the walls.
Around Jaanipäev (23-24 June) the whole country shuts down and heads to bonfires - book accommodation early, expect closures.
Sauna etiquette: it's a serious, usually nude, single-sex ritual - shower first and ask before throwing water.
Ferries to Saaremaa/Hiiumaa (praamid.ee) sell out for cars on summer weekends - reserve ahead.
Tipping ~10% is appreciated but genuinely optional.
Estonia is the priciest Baltic state; Tartu and the islands are notably cheaper than Tallinn.

Latvia.best_time_note: June-August for beach weather in Jūrmala and midsummer Jāņi festivities; September paints Gauja NP in superb autumn colour.

rail.note: New electric trains make Riga-Jūrmala (~€1.50) and Riga-Sigulda dirt cheap; buy in the app or at machines, no reservations needed.

bus.note: Comfortable coaches connect Riga with Vilnius and Tallinn from ~€10-15; domestic minibuses reach Kuldīga and Kolka cheaply.

driving.tolls: No vignette or tolls for cars; a small entry fee applies to drive into Jūrmala resort in summer (~€3/day).
warnings: Headlights mandatory 24/7
Winter tyres compulsory Dec-Mar
Gravel roads common once off main highways - allow extra time
driving.car_recommended_for: Cape Kolka and Livonian coast villages, Kuldīga, Latgale lakeland - rural buses are sparse
driving.car_not_needed_in: Riga, Jūrmala, Sigulda and Cēsis, all linked by cheap trains

must_see.name: Riga Old Town & Art Nouveau district
must_see.why: House of the Blackheads plus Alberta iela, Europe's densest Art Nouveau street - free to admire.

must_see.name: Riga Central Market
must_see.why: Vast market in WWI Zeppelin hangars - the cheapest lunch and smoked-fish tasting in the capital.

must_see.name: Jūrmala
must_see.why: 33 km of white-sand beach and wooden villas, 30 minutes and ~€1.50 by train from Riga.

must_see.name: Sigulda & Gauja National Park
must_see.why: Castle ruins, bobsled track rides and forested river valleys - Latvia's 'Switzerland'.

must_see.name: Cēsis
must_see.why: Medieval castle you explore by candle-lantern, in one of Latvia's prettiest small towns.

must_see.name: Rundāle Palace
must_see.why: Baltic Versailles by the architect of St Petersburg's Winter Palace.

must_see.name: Kuldīga
must_see.why: UNESCO-listed old town beside Europe's widest waterfall (Ventas rumba); watch fish leap it in spring.

must_see.name: Liepāja & Karosta
must_see.why: Beach city with an eerie abandoned tsarist-Soviet naval base and prison you can tour.

must_see.name: Cape Kolka
must_see.why: Where the Gulf of Riga meets the open Baltic, amid tiny Livonian fishing villages.

must_see.name: Aglona & Latgale lakes
must_see.why: Pilgrimage basilica and blue-lake countryside in Latvia's least-visited, cheapest region.

insights: Latvia uses the euro; cards work almost everywhere, but keep coins for rural markets.
At Riga airport skip the taxi touts - Bolt to the centre costs around €8-12.
Decline DCC on terminals and avoid Euronet ATMs, common in the Old Town.
Old Town Riga bars have a history of tourist overcharging - check prices before ordering rounds.
Riga Central Market and Miera iela cafés eat far better and cheaper than Old Town terraces.
Jāņi midsummer (23-24 June) shuts shops and empties cities - join a countryside celebration if invited.
Tipping ~10% for good service; often a service charge already appears on Riga bills.
Balzams: try Riga Black Balsam in currant form before committing to the raw original.

Lithuania.best_time_note: June-July for the Curonian Spit and lake swimming; September keeps mild weather, low prices and mushroom-foraging forests.

rail.note: Cheap and modernising fast: Vilnius-Kaunas from ~€6-8 runs hourly-ish, Vilnius-Klaipėda ~€20; buy in the app, no seat-price games.

bus.note: Dense domestic network (Autobusubilietai.lt) plus comfortable international coaches to Riga and Warsaw from ~€10.

driving.tolls: No vignette or tolls for cars on public roads; the Curonian Spit charges a car entry/ecology fee after the Klaipėda ferry (in the tens of euros in high season).
warnings: Headlights mandatory 24/7
Winter tyres compulsory 10 Nov-31 Mar
Strict speed camera network on the A1 Vilnius-Klaipėda highway
driving.car_recommended_for: Curonian Spit villages, Hill of Crosses, Aukštaitija and Dzūkija lakes and forests
driving.car_not_needed_in: Vilnius, Kaunas and Klaipėda, all connected by cheap fast trains

must_see.name: Vilnius Old Town & Užupis
must_see.why: Baroque UNESCO old town beside a self-declared bohemian 'republic' with its own constitution.

must_see.name: Trakai Island Castle
must_see.why: Red-brick lake castle 30 minutes from Vilnius; try Karaite kibinai pastries on the shore.

must_see.name: Curonian Spit (Nida)
must_see.why: UNESCO dune peninsula of pine forests and the 'Baltic Sahara' at Parnidis dune.

must_see.name: Kaunas
must_see.why: Interwar modernist architecture (UNESCO 2023), street art and cheaper beds than Vilnius.

must_see.name: Hill of Crosses
must_see.why: Hundreds of thousands of crosses on one hillock - one of Europe's most haunting pilgrimage sites.

must_see.name: Klaipėda
must_see.why: Germanic-flavoured port town, gateway ferry to the Spit, with a lively sea festival.

must_see.name: Aukštaitija National Park
must_see.why: 126 lakes for canoeing between wooden villages and an old beekeeping museum.

must_see.name: Kernavė
must_see.why: UNESCO mound-fort site of Lithuania's medieval capital, atmospheric and free.

must_see.name: Druskininkai
must_see.why: Affordable spa town with a huge indoor water park and the offbeat Grūtas Park of Soviet statues.

must_see.name: Anykščiai
must_see.why: Treetop walking path, narrow-gauge railway and sandstone outcrops in gentle lake country.

insights: Lithuania uses the euro and is largely cashless - Bolt covers taxis and scooters in all main cities.
The Klaipėda-Smiltynė ferry is the only road link to the Curonian Spit; foot passengers cross cheaply, cars pay ferry plus an entry fee.
Šaltibarščiai (cold pink beet soup) season is summer - most canteens serve it with hot potatoes for ~€3.
Cheap 'canteen' chains (e.g. self-service valgykla) do full meals for €5-7.
Tipping ~10% for table service; not expected at counters.
Joninės midsummer (24 June) is a public holiday - transport thins out and coastal beds sell out.
Book Nida accommodation well ahead in July-August; visiting the Spit as a Klaipėda day trip is the budget option.
Avoid DCC and Euronet ATMs in Vilnius Old Town, as elsewhere in the region.

Germany.best_time_note: May-June and September bring warm, less crowded weather; December is magical for Christmas markets.

rail.note: Book Sparpreis fares early (from ~EUR 18 long-distance); the Deutschlandticket (EUR 63/month in 2026) covers ALL regional trains, trams and buses nationwide - superb value for multi-city trips.

bus.note: FlixBus dominates intercity buses and is often the cheapest way between big cities if booked ahead.

driving.tolls: No tolls for cars on the Autobahn; only a couple of private tunnels (e.g. Warnow, Herrentunnel) charge small fees.
warnings: Many city centres are Umweltzonen - a green Umweltplakette sticker (~EUR 5-20, order before travel) is mandatory even for foreign cars
Autobahn sections without limit still have a 130 km/h advisory speed; left lane is strictly for overtaking
Rettungsgasse (emergency corridor) is compulsory in traffic jams - fines are steep
driving.car_recommended_for: Black Forest, Saxon Switzerland, Romantic Road villages, Baltic coast and Alpine backroads
driving.car_not_needed_in: Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Cologne and any city trip - the Deutschlandticket makes regional rail trivial

must_see.name: Berlin
must_see.why: Wall history, world-class free-ish museums and Europe's best nightlife in one sprawling capital.

must_see.name: Munich & Neuschwanstein
must_see.why: Beer-garden culture plus the fairytale castle that inspired Disney, an easy day trip away.

must_see.name: Saxon Switzerland
must_see.why: Bastei bridge sandstone pinnacles above the Elbe - Germany's most dramatic hiking, near Dresden.

must_see.name: Rhine Valley (Bacharach-St. Goar)
must_see.why: UNESCO gorge of castles and vineyards, best seen from the slow river ferry or Riesling terraces.

must_see.name: Black Forest
must_see.why: Cuckoo-clock villages, Triberg waterfalls and dense pine ridges made for road trips and cake stops.

must_see.name: Dresden
must_see.why: Baroque Altstadt rebuilt from rubble, with the Zwinger and Frauenkirche - cheaper than western cities.

must_see.name: Hamburg
must_see.why: Speicherstadt warehouses, Elbphilharmonie plaza (free) and a gritty-cool harbour vibe.

must_see.name: Cologne Cathedral
must_see.why: Germany's most visited landmark, free to enter, right beside the main station.

must_see.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
must_see.why: The best-preserved walled medieval town in the country; walk the ramparts at dawn before tour buses.

must_see.name: Berchtesgaden & Koenigssee
must_see.why: Emerald fjord-like lake and the Eagle's Nest in Germany's Alpine corner.

must_see.name: Bamberg
must_see.why: UNESCO old town famous for smoked Rauchbier and canal-side 'Little Venice', skipped by most tourists.

must_see.name: Ruegen
must_see.why: Chalk cliffs of Jasmund and Baltic beach resorts - Germany's favourite domestic escape.

insights: Cash is still king in many bakeries, kiosks and smaller restaurants - carry EUR 50-100; cards can be refused even in Berlin.
Almost everything closes on Sundays (Ruhetag) except restaurants, bakeries (mornings) and station shops - plan grocery runs on Saturday.
City taxes vary: Berlin charges 7.5% of the net room price, Hamburg and Frankfurt have per-night culture taxes; budget ~5-8% extra on accommodation.
Bottle deposit (Pfand) is EUR 0.25 on most plastic bottles/cans - return them at any supermarket machine.
Ryanair from Belgium serves Berlin, Cologne/Weeze, Hamburg, Nuremberg and Memmingen (gateway to Bavaria/Alps).
Tap water is safe but restaurants rarely serve it free - ordering 'Leitungswasser' works but expect side-eye.
Validate regional train tickets where required and always carry ID; on-board fines are EUR 60.
Lunch menus (Mittagstisch) at EUR 9-13 are the cheap way to eat well; dinner at the same place can cost double.

Austria.best_time_note: June and September are ideal for Alpine hiking without peak crowds; December for Christmas markets, February for ski deals.

rail.note: Sparschiene advance fares start around EUR 10-15; on Vienna-Salzburg the private competitor Westbahn is often cheaper with no reservation needed.

bus.note: FlixBus links Vienna, Salzburg and Graz cheaply; OeBB Postbus reaches Alpine valleys trains skip.

driving.vignette: Vignette required on motorways: EUR 12.80/10 days, EUR 32/2 months, EUR 106.80/year (2026); buy digital at shop.asfinag.at with instant validity.
driving.tolls: Extra Sondermaut on top of the vignette for Brenner, Tauern, Arlberg and other Alpine tunnels/passes (roughly EUR 10-30 per crossing).
warnings: Winter tyres are mandatory in wintry conditions 1 Nov-15 Apr
IG-L environmental speed limits (100 km/h) on some motorways are camera-enforced
Grossglockner High Alpine Road is a separate private toll (~EUR 45/car)
driving.car_recommended_for: Salzkammergut lakes, Grossglockner, Tyrolean side valleys and the Wachau at your own pace
driving.car_not_needed_in: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck and Graz - trains and city transit cover them completely

must_see.name: Vienna
must_see.why: Imperial palaces, coffee-house culture and world-class museums - one of Europe's most liveable capitals.

must_see.name: Salzburg
must_see.why: Mozart's baroque old town beneath the Hohensalzburg fortress, with Sound of Music scenery all around.

must_see.name: Hallstatt
must_see.why: The postcard lakeside village; arrive before 9am or sleep over to dodge day-trip crowds.

must_see.name: Wachau Valley
must_see.why: Danube terraced-vineyard gorge between Melk and Krems - cycle it and stop at Duernstein castle ruin.

must_see.name: Innsbruck
must_see.why: A genuine city in the Alps: Nordkette cable car takes you from old town to 2,300 m in 30 minutes.

must_see.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road
must_see.why: Austria's highest pass road with glacier views of its tallest peak.

must_see.name: Salzkammergut lakes
must_see.why: Wolfgangsee and Gosausee offer swimmable Alpine water and easy trails, far cheaper than Switzerland.

must_see.name: Graz
must_see.why: UNESCO old town, buzzing food scene and few foreign tourists - Austria's underrated second city.

must_see.name: Zillertal & Mayrhofen
must_see.why: Classic Tyrolean valley for hiking, via ferrata and the Hintertux year-round glacier.

must_see.name: Semmering Railway
must_see.why: UNESCO 1854 mountain railway you can ride on a normal OeBB ticket from Vienna.

must_see.name: Bregenz & Bregenzerwald
must_see.why: Lake Constance floating opera stage plus timber-architecture villages and cheese dairies.

insights: Vienna's Ortstaxe is 3.2% of the net room rate until 30 Jun 2026, rising to 5% from 1 Jul 2026; Alpine resorts charge Kurtaxe of ~EUR 1-4 per person/night instead.
Shops close Sundays and often by 18:00 Saturdays; station and airport supermarkets are the exception.
Tap water is excellent and served free with coffee in traditional cafes - a rarity in Europe.
Mountain huts (Huetten) offer beds from ~EUR 25-35 with Alpine club discount; book summer weekends well ahead.
Ryanair flies from Charleroi/Brussels to Vienna; for Tyrol, Memmingen or Salzburg (seasonal) can be closer than flying to Vienna.
Many ski areas and lake regions give a free guest card (with tourist tax) covering local buses and lifts - ask your host.
A Stempel culture survives: validate bus/tram tickets on board or risk EUR 105 fines in Vienna.

Switzerland.best_time_note: Mid-June to September for open hiking trails and cable cars; September has the clearest mountain views and thinner crowds.

rail.note: Supersaver tickets (up to 70% off) appear ~2 weeks ahead; the Half Fare Card (~CHF 120/month for visitors) or Swiss Travel Pass pays off fast since full fares are brutal.

bus.note: Yellow PostBuses reach every mountain village and are covered by Swiss rail passes; FlixBus handles cheap international arrivals.

driving.vignette: Vignette required: CHF 40 (~EUR 42) flat, valid 1 Dec 2025-31 Jan 2027 for the 2026 year; buy the e-vignette per number plate at via.admin.ch.
driving.tolls: Motorways covered by the vignette; separate fees only for car-carrying tunnels/trains like Grand St Bernard, Munt la Schera and Vereina.
warnings: Speeding fines are income-linked and severe - even 5 km/h over in town costs CHF 40+, radar tolerance is tiny
Many Alpine passes (Furka, Grimsel, Susten) close roughly Oct-May
Car-free resorts (Zermatt, Wengen, Muerren) require parking at valley stations
driving.car_recommended_for: Remote valleys (Val Verzasca, Appenzell backroads) and multi-pass road trips - otherwise trains beat driving
driving.car_not_needed_in: Basically everywhere: Swiss public transport is the world's best and reaches trailheads by PostBus

must_see.name: Lauterbrunnen & Jungfrau region
must_see.why: 72-waterfall valley beneath Eiger and Jungfrau; hike Muerren-Grindelwald instead of buying the pricey Jungfraujoch ticket.

must_see.name: Zermatt & the Matterhorn
must_see.why: The iconic pyramid peak from a car-free village; the 5-Seenweg trail gives the classic reflections.

must_see.name: Lucerne & Mt Pilatus
must_see.why: Chapel Bridge, lake steamers and a golden-round-trip mountain combo all in half a day from the city.

must_see.name: Aletsch Glacier
must_see.why: The Alps' largest glacier, seen from easy ridge trails above Bettmeralp - UNESCO and far quieter than Jungfraujoch.

must_see.name: Lavaux vineyards
must_see.why: UNESCO terraced vines above Lake Geneva; the Lutry-St-Saphorin walk with wine stops costs almost nothing.

must_see.name: Bern
must_see.why: Arcaded UNESCO old town where locals float down the Aare river past parliament in summer - free fun.

must_see.name: Val Verzasca & Ticino
must_see.why: Emerald pools, Roman bridges and Italian-speaking palm-tree Switzerland around Lugano and Locarno.

must_see.name: Bernina Express line
must_see.why: UNESCO rail route over 2,253 m to Italy - ride it with a normal regional ticket instead of the panoramic supplement.

must_see.name: Appenzell & Ebenalp
must_see.why: Painted village, cliffside Aescher inn and the Seealpsee - old Switzerland in miniature.

must_see.name: Creux du Van
must_see.why: A 160 m natural rock amphitheatre in the Jura, spectacular and nearly tourist-free.

must_see.name: Geneva & Lake Geneva
must_see.why: Jet d'Eau, old town and easy lakeside trains to Montreux and Chillon Castle.

insights: Budget CHF 25-35 for a plain restaurant main; self-cater via Coop/Migros/Denner and use their CHF 10-15 lunch buffets and pre-6pm discounts.
Tap water is superb and public fountains are everywhere - refill instead of buying CHF 5 bottles.
Hostels and mountain huts run CHF 40-70/night; many guest cards (via Kurtaxe of CHF 2-7/night) include free local transport.
Pay in CHF: euros are accepted in some shops but at poor rates with CHF change.
Ryanair does not serve Switzerland well - fly to Basel-Mulhouse (EuroAirport) with other carriers or train in from Germany/France.
Supermarkets close Sundays except at major stations and airports.
Buy cable-car tickets online day-of for frequent 10-20% web discounts, and check SBB supersaver fares before any long ride.
Picnicking is culturally normal - grills and free firewood at official Feuerstelle spots make the cheapest Alpine dinners.

Liechtenstein.best_time_note: June to September for high trails like the Fuerstensteig; January-March if you want Malbun's tiny, cheap-for-the-region ski area.

rail.note: Only a few trains stop at Schaan-Vaduz; practically everyone arrives by bus from Swiss rail hubs Sargans or Buchs SG, or from Feldkirch in Austria.

bus.note: The lime-green LIEmobil network covers the whole country; a day pass costs only a few francs and Sargans-Vaduz takes ~30 min.

driving.tolls: No motorways or tolls inside Liechtenstein, but you need a Swiss vignette (CHF 40) if you arrive via Swiss motorways.
warnings: Swiss traffic rules and strict speed enforcement apply in practice
The Malbun road is Alpine - winter tyres needed in snow
driving.car_recommended_for: Combining Liechtenstein with Graubuenden or Vorarlberg road trips
driving.car_not_needed_in: The whole country - LIEmobil buses reach every village including Malbun

must_see.name: Vaduz Castle viewpoint
must_see.why: The prince's residence isn't open, but the short trail up gives the classic castle-over-Rhine-valley photo.

must_see.name: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein
must_see.why: A serious modern-art collection in a striking black cube - the cultural highlight of the capital.

must_see.name: Fuerstensteig trail
must_see.why: Exposed ridge path on the Drei Schwestern massif; one of the Alps' great short via-ferrata-style hikes.

must_see.name: Malbun
must_see.why: The country's only ski resort at 1,600 m - family-scale, and lovely for summer chairlift hikes to Sareis.

must_see.name: Gutenberg Castle
must_see.why: A fully preserved hilltop castle with free grounds, prettier and quieter than Vaduz's.

must_see.name: Triesenberg & Walser villages
must_see.why: Hillside hamlets founded by Walser settlers, with a small museum and huge valley views.

must_see.name: Eschnerberg trail
must_see.why: Easy panoramic ridge walk linking historic lowland villages - good rain-or-shine option.

must_see.name: Vaduz Treasure Chamber & stamp museum
must_see.why: Crown jewels, Faberge eggs and the famous stamps - quirky micro-state history in 30 minutes.

insights: Swiss francs are the currency but euros are widely accepted at approximate 1:1 rates - change comes in CHF.
No airport or Ryanair route: cheapest approach from Belgium is flying to Memmingen or Friedrichshafen, or rail via Zurich to Sargans.
The whole country is doable as a day trip from Feldkirch or Sargans, but staying overnight earns you a quiet Alpine evening and the Adventure Pass discounts.
Prices match Switzerland - budget CHF 20+ for a simple lunch; the Migros in Vaduz/Schaan is the self-catering fallback.
A souvenir passport stamp costs CHF 3 at the Vaduz tourist office.
Buses stop running relatively early in the evening - check the last Malbun departure.
food: Prince of Liechtenstein wines from the Hofkellerei
events: Staatsfeiertag national day with castle-meadow party and fireworks (15 Aug)

Netherlands.best_time_note: April-May for tulips and King's Day energy; June and September give the best cycling weather without peak-summer crowds.

rail.note: No advance-purchase discounts domestically - fares are fixed and distance-based; check in/out with a contactless bank card (OVpay) and look for off-peak group deals and supermarket promo tickets.

bus.note: FlixBus from Brussels/Antwerp to Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Eindhoven is usually far cheaper than international rail.

driving.tolls: Essentially none: the Westerscheldetunnel became toll-free for cars in early 2025; only the small Kiltunnel near Dordrecht still charges.
warnings: Cyclists have priority nearly everywhere - always check bike lanes before turning or opening doors
Parking in Amsterdam runs up to ~EUR 7.50/hour; use P+R garages on the edge for a few euros/day with transit included
Several city centres have milieuzones banning older diesels
driving.car_recommended_for: Zeeland Delta Works, Giethoorn, Texel and Hoge Veluwe - rural sights with thin transit
driving.car_not_needed_in: Amsterdam, Utrecht, Rotterdam, The Hague - trains every 10-15 min plus rental bikes beat any car

must_see.name: Amsterdam canal ring
must_see.why: UNESCO canals, the Rijksmuseum and Anne Frank House - book the latter online exactly 6 weeks ahead.

must_see.name: Hoge Veluwe & Kroeller-Mueller
must_see.why: Free white bikes through heathland to the world's second-largest Van Gogh collection.

must_see.name: Utrecht
must_see.why: Amsterdam's canal charm with wharf-level cafes and a fraction of the tourists.

must_see.name: Kinderdijk
must_see.why: Nineteen UNESCO windmills in a row - cycle in free along the dike instead of paying for the boat.

must_see.name: Keukenhof & bulb fields
must_see.why: Seven million tulips, mid-March to mid-May only; rent a bike to tour the surrounding fields free.

must_see.name: Giethoorn
must_see.why: Car-free canal village best seen from a rented whisper-boat, early morning before tour groups.

must_see.name: Texel & the Wadden Sea
must_see.why: Ferry-hop to dunes, seals and UNESCO mudflat-walking (wadlopen) with a guide.

must_see.name: Maastricht
must_see.why: Burgundian cafe culture, hill country and Europe's prettiest bookshop in a Gothic church.

must_see.name: Rotterdam
must_see.why: Cube houses, Markthal and Europe's biggest port - the architectural counterpoint to Amsterdam.

must_see.name: Zeeland Delta Works
must_see.why: Storm-surge mega-engineering plus wide North Sea beaches an easy hop from Belgium.

must_see.name: Haarlem
must_see.why: Grote Markt, Frans Hals and proper brown cafes 15 minutes from Amsterdam at lower room rates.

insights: Amsterdam charges Europe's highest tourist tax: 12.5% of the room price, and national VAT on accommodation jumped from 9% to 21% in 2026 - total tax ~33.5%, so sleep in Haarlem or Utrecht.
Never walk in the bike lane (reddish asphalt); bikes won't stop and locals will yell.
Many shops/restaurants are PIN-only (debit); some places refuse credit cards AND cash - carry a debit card that works abroad.
Check in AND out with your contactless bank card on all trains, trams and buses (OVpay) or you pay a full-route fare.
Museumkaart (~EUR 79.90/year) pays off in 4-5 museum visits if you'll return within weeks; otherwise book timed tickets online.
Monday mornings many shops open only at 12:00-13:00; supermarkets are open Sundays in cities, unlike Germany.
From Belgium the train (Brussels-Amsterdam) is often easier than flying; Ryanair also serves Eindhoven from Charleroi.
events: King's Day nationwide street party (27 Apr)

Belgium.best_time_note: May-June and September for terrace weather and festivals; late April for the Hallerbos bluebells; December for Christmas markets in Brussels and Ghent.

rail.note: Weekend Tickets are roughly half price for any return Fri evening-Sun; under-26s ride almost anywhere cheap with the Youth Multi 10-trip pass, and Standard Multi cuts costs for everyone else.

bus.note: FlixBus covers international hops; De Lijn (Flanders), TEC (Wallonia) and STIB (Brussels) run dense, cheap regional networks including the coast tram.

driving.tolls: None for cars except the Liefkenshoek tunnel in Antwerp (~EUR 6-8); trucks pay km-charges instead.
warnings: Brussels, Antwerp and Ghent are Low Emission Zones - even compliant foreign cars may need free online registration or face EUR 150+ fines
Priority-from-the-right applies on many unmarked urban junctions
Antwerp and Brussels ring roads jam badly at rush hour - time trips around them
driving.car_recommended_for: The Ardennes (Bouillon, La Roche, Han caves) and abbey-hopping in Wallonia where rail is sparse
driving.car_not_needed_in: Brussels, Ghent, Bruges, Antwerp, Leuven - all linked by frequent trains, and the coast by tram

must_see.name: Ghent
must_see.why: Gravensteen castle, the Mystic Lamb altarpiece and canalside nightlife - Bruges' beauty with real local life.

must_see.name: Bruges
must_see.why: The perfectly preserved medieval canal city; stay overnight to see it empty after the day-trippers leave.

must_see.name: Antwerp
must_see.why: Rubens, the world's most beautiful railway station and Belgium's best fashion and food scene.

must_see.name: Brussels Grand Place & museums
must_see.why: The gilded main square plus Magritte and comic-strip culture; many museums are free the first Sunday/Wednesday of the month.

must_see.name: Dinant & the Meuse
must_see.why: Citadel-topped cliff town, kayaking on the Lesse and the birthplace of the saxophone.

must_see.name: Ardennes (Bouillon & La Roche)
must_see.why: Castles, forests and river valleys - Belgium's wilderness for hiking and kayak weekends.

must_see.name: Hallerbos
must_see.why: A purple carpet of bluebells for about two weeks in mid-late April - free and easy from Brussels.

must_see.name: Leuven
must_see.why: Flamboyant town hall, the Oude Markt 'longest bar in Europe' and Stella's brewery city.

must_see.name: Belgian coast & Kusttram
must_see.why: The world's longest tram line links all 68 km of beach towns from De Panne to Knokke.

must_see.name: Han-sur-Lesse caves
must_see.why: Belgium's most impressive cave system paired with a drive-through wildlife park.

must_see.name: Mechelen
must_see.why: St Rumbold's tower climb and a moving Holocaust museum, overlooked between Brussels and Antwerp.

must_see.name: Tournai
must_see.why: Five-towered UNESCO cathedral and Belgium's oldest belfry, minutes from Ryanair's Charleroi side of the country.

insights: This is home turf: Weekend Tickets (about 50% off) and B-Excursion combo fares make domestic city trips cheaper than driving and parking.
City taxes exist at home too: Bruges and Antwerp charge roughly EUR 2.5-3.5 per person/night, Brussels ~EUR 4-9 depending on hotel class.
Museums almost universally close on Mondays; big attractions in Bruges/Ghent sell timed tickets - book summer weekends ahead.
Frituur etiquette: order a 'friet met stoofvleessaus' once in your life; fries are a meal, not a side.
Each beer has its own glass and its own strength - Westvleteren and other Trappists from 8-12% sneak up on you.
If driving to a Belgian city, register your plate for the Brussels/Antwerp/Ghent LEZ even in a compliant car - foreign-plated Belgians returning with rentals get fined too.
The coast tram day pass (~EUR 7.5) is the cheapest seaside day out in the country.

Luxembourg.best_time_note: May-June and September for hiking the Mullerthal; October adds autumn colour to the castle valleys and Moselle harvest season.

rail.note: ALL domestic trains, trams and buses have been free nationwide since 2020 - no ticket needed; you only pay for 1st class or cross-border legs to Trier, Arlon or Metz.

bus.note: Free RGTR buses reach every village including Vianden and the Mullerthal trailheads; plan with the mobiliteit.lu app.

driving.tolls: None - and fuel is among the cheapest in Western Europe, so cross-border drivers traditionally fill up here.
warnings: Luxembourg City parking is scarce and pricey - use free P+R lots with the free tram instead
Rush-hour traffic from French/Belgian/German commuters is heavy on all approach motorways
driving.car_recommended_for: A castles-and-Moselle loop (Vianden, Bourscheid, Beaufort, wine villages) in a single day
driving.car_not_needed_in: The entire country if you have mild patience - free public transport covers every corner

must_see.name: Luxembourg City old town & Bock Casemates
must_see.why: UNESCO fortress tunnels and the dramatic Grund lower town, with the free Pfaffenthal panoramic lift.

must_see.name: Vianden Castle
must_see.why: One of Europe's finest restored medieval castles, above a riverside town with a chairlift viewpoint.

must_see.name: Mullerthal 'Little Switzerland'
must_see.why: Mossy sandstone gorges and the Schiessentuempel waterfall on the 112 km Mullerthal Trail - all free.

must_see.name: Moselle wine valley
must_see.why: Cremant and Riesling tastings in Remich and Schengen - yes, that Schengen, with its EU museum.

must_see.name: Esch-sur-Sure
must_see.why: A near-island village wrapped in a loop of the Sauer river beneath a ruined castle.

must_see.name: Clervaux
must_see.why: Home of Edward Steichen's 'The Family of Man', one of photography's landmark exhibitions, in a white castle.

must_see.name: Beaufort Castle
must_see.why: Atmospheric medieval ruin plus Renaissance chateau at the edge of the best Mullerthal hikes.

must_see.name: Echternach
must_see.why: The country's oldest town, a grand abbey and a lake loop - the natural Mullerthal base.

must_see.name: Minett/Belval blast furnaces
must_see.why: A steelworks turned sci-fi university campus - industrial heritage you can climb at sunset.

insights: Public transport is 100% free nationwide (since 2020) - the only such country in the world; skip the rental car unless castle-hopping on a tight schedule.
Fuel, tobacco and alcohol are notably cheaper than in Belgium - Belgians routinely detour to fill the tank.
Hotel prices in the capital are business-driven: weekends are cheaper than weekdays, the reverse of most cities.
Restaurant mains run EUR 20-30; the plat du jour at lunch or bakery sandwiches keep budgets sane.
Luxembourg City empties on Sundays; that's the best day for the free walking circuits (Wenzel route) and casemates.
No Ryanair from Belgium (it's a 2h drive/train from Brussels); from home, direct CFL/SNCB trains to Luxembourg City are simplest.
Most trails and castles cluster within 45 min of the capital - a car-free weekend covers a surprising amount.
food: Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked pork with broad beans)
events: Echternach dancing procession, UNESCO-listed (Whit Tuesday, May/Jun)

United Kingdom.best_time_note: May, June and September give the driest, brightest weather without August school-holiday crowds and prices.

rail.note: Book Advance fares weeks ahead (walk-up prices are brutal); Railcards give 1/3 off and split-ticketing apps like TrainSplit cut costs further.

bus.note: Intercity coaches are far cheaper than trains, with Megabus/FlixBus fares from a few pounds if booked early.

driving.tolls: Almost no tolls: M6 Toll ~EUR 11 (GBP 9.70), Dartford Crossing ~EUR 3 (GBP 2.50, pay online by midnight next day).
warnings: London Congestion Charge is GBP 18/day (~EUR 21) since Jan 2026, EVs no longer exempt; ULEZ adds GBP 12.50 (~EUR 14.50) for non-compliant cars, so up to ~EUR 35/day combined
Driving is on the left with mostly manual rentals; automatics cost more
Single-track roads with passing places in the Scottish Highlands and rural Wales
Many cities have bus lanes and box junctions enforced by camera with fines by post
driving.car_recommended_for: Scottish Highlands and islands, Lake District, Snowdonia, Cotswolds and Cornwall
driving.car_not_needed_in: London, Edinburgh, Manchester and other cities; intercity rail links them well

must_see.name: Edinburgh Old Town & Arthur's Seat
must_see.why: Medieval Royal Mile, castle and an extinct volcano you can climb inside the city.

must_see.name: Isle of Skye
must_see.why: Old Man of Storr, Quiraing and Fairy Pools pack Scotland's most dramatic scenery onto one island.

must_see.name: Lake District
must_see.why: England's best hiking around Windermere, Keswick and Scafell Pike, a UNESCO landscape.

must_see.name: York
must_see.why: Intact city walls, the Shambles and York Minster make it England's best-preserved medieval city.

must_see.name: Bath
must_see.why: Roman baths and honey-coloured Georgian crescents, all walkable and UNESCO-listed.

must_see.name: Snowdonia (Eryri)
must_see.why: Climb or take the rack railway up Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon), with slate villages and zip lines nearby.

must_see.name: Giant's Causeway
must_see.why: 40,000 basalt columns on the Antrim coast, paired with the Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge.

must_see.name: Cotswolds
must_see.why: Postcard stone villages like Bibury and Castle Combe strung along gentle walking trails.

must_see.name: Cornwall (St Ives & Land's End)
must_see.why: Surf beaches, coastal path and the theatrical clifftop Minack Theatre.

must_see.name: Durdle Door & Jurassic Coast
must_see.why: A natural limestone arch on a fossil-rich UNESCO coastline, best at sunrise.

must_see.name: Peak District
must_see.why: Underrated gritstone edges and stately Chatsworth, easily reached from Manchester or Sheffield.

insights: EU citizens need a UK ETA: GBP 20 (~EUR 23) since 8 Apr 2026 (was GBP 16), valid 2 years for unlimited visits up to 6 months; apply via the UK ETA app, usually approved in minutes to 3 days.
EU national ID cards are NOT accepted; you must travel on a passport.
The UK uses pounds, not euros; contactless cards work everywhere and London transport caps daily fares automatically (no Oyster needed).
Book long-distance trains 4-12 weeks ahead; same-day fares can cost 3-4x more.
Many national museums (British Museum, National Gallery, Tate) are completely free.
Tipping: 10-12.5% in sit-down restaurants (often added as 'service charge'); never tip at the pub bar.
Sunday rail engineering works are common; check journeys and allow buffer time to Stansted/Luton for Ryanair flights.
Pubs: order and pay at the bar; kitchens often close early (~21:00).

Ireland.best_time_note: May-June bring the most sunshine and long evenings; September is quieter with mild weather, while rain is possible year-round.

rail.note: Online advance fares are much cheaper than station prices; the network is Dublin-centric, so cross-country trips often route via Dublin.

bus.note: Private coaches (Citylink, GoBus, Dublin Coach) are often faster and cheaper than trains, e.g. Dublin-Galway from ~EUR 10-15.

driving.tolls: M50 Dublin ring is barrier-free (~EUR 3.70/pass, pay at eflow.ie by 20:00 next day or fines apply); other motorway tolls EUR 1.60-3.10 at booths.
