warnings: Drive on the left; rentals are manual by default and Irish CDW insurance excess is notoriously high, check card coverage
Rural roads (Ring of Kerry, Connemara) are narrow with stone walls and tour buses; drive the Ring of Kerry anti-clockwise like the buses
M50 toll has no booths, forgetting to pay online triggers escalating penalties on rental cars
driving.car_recommended_for: Wild Atlantic Way, Ring of Kerry, Dingle, Connemara and Donegal
driving.car_not_needed_in: Dublin, Cork and Galway city centres; Dublin is fully walkable with Leap Card transit

must_see.name: Cliffs of Moher
must_see.why: 214 m Atlantic cliffs; arrive before 10:00 or after 17:00 to dodge coach crowds.

must_see.name: Ring of Kerry & Killarney NP
must_see.why: Ireland's classic 179 km loop of lakes, mountains and coast around Killarney.

must_see.name: Dingle Peninsula
must_see.why: Slea Head Drive rivals the Ring of Kerry with fewer buses, plus a lively pub town.

must_see.name: Galway & Connemara
must_see.why: Buzzing bohemian city gateway to Connemara's bogs, loughs and Kylemore Abbey.

must_see.name: Trinity College & Book of Kells
must_see.why: The 9th-century illuminated gospel and the stunning Long Room library.

must_see.name: Aran Islands (Inis Mór)
must_see.why: Cycle to the clifftop fort of Dún Aonghasa on an Irish-speaking island.

must_see.name: Glendalough & Wicklow Mountains
must_see.why: Monastic round tower in a glacial valley, an easy day trip from Dublin.

must_see.name: Slieve League (Sliabh Liag)
must_see.why: Sea cliffs nearly three times higher than Moher, with a fraction of the visitors.

must_see.name: Kilkenny
must_see.why: Compact medieval mile with a castle, cathedral and craft-beer scene.

must_see.name: Cobh & Cork
must_see.why: Titanic's last port of call, the English Market and nearby Blarney Castle.

insights: No ETA or visa for EU citizens, Ireland is EU and you can enter with a national ID card (unlike the UK); note it is NOT in Schengen.
Ryanair's home country: Dublin is its biggest base, with Cork, Shannon and Knock also served from Belgium.
A Leap Visitor Card caps Dublin transport costs (EUR 8/24h, EUR 16/72h) including airport buses.

Crossing into Northern Ireland (Giant's Causeway, Belfast) is seamless with no border checks, but it uses pounds and technically requires the UK ETA for EU citizens (in practice there are no routine checks on the land border).
Tipping: ~10% in restaurants for good service; not expected in pubs.
Weather flips fast, pack rain layers even in July; many attractions are outdoors.
Cards are accepted nearly everywhere; look for free traditional music sessions in pubs (Doolin, Dingle, Galway).

Iceland.best_time_note: June-August offer midnight sun, open highland roads and the best weather; September adds northern lights with lower prices.

rail.note: Iceland has no railways at all; get around by rental car, tour buses or the limited Strætó public bus network.

bus.note: Strætó covers Reykjavik and some intercity routes, but rural service is sparse, most travellers self-drive or join tours.

driving.tolls: Only the Vaðlaheiði tunnel near Akureyri (~EUR 12-15, pay online at tunnel.is within 24h); no other road tolls.
warnings: F-roads (highland routes) legally require a 4x4, open only ~late June to September, and river crossings void most insurance
Off-road driving is illegal with heavy fines; single-lane bridges and blind crests are common on the Ring Road
Weather can close roads any month, check road.is and safetravel.is daily; sandstorms can strip paint (get gravel/sand insurance)
Sneaker waves at Reynisfjara beach have killed tourists, obey warning signs
driving.car_recommended_for: The Ring Road, Snæfellsnes, Westfjords and any itinerary beyond Reykjavik and Golden Circle tours
driving.car_not_needed_in: Reykjavik itself; Golden Circle, south coast and Blue Lagoon are all doable by day tour or Flybus

must_see.name: Golden Circle (Þingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss)
must_see.why: Rift valley between tectonic plates, erupting Strokkur geyser and a two-tier waterfall in one loop.

must_see.name: Jökulsárlón & Diamond Beach
must_see.why: Icebergs calve into a lagoon and wash up glittering on black sand.

must_see.name: Seljalandsfoss & Skógafoss
must_see.why: Walk behind one waterfall and climb beside the other, minutes apart on Route 1.

must_see.name: Reynisfjara & Vík
must_see.why: Black-sand beach with basalt columns and sea stacks beneath puffin cliffs.

must_see.name: Snæfellsnes Peninsula
must_see.why: 'Iceland in miniature': Kirkjufell mountain, lava fields, seal beaches and a glacier-capped volcano.

must_see.name: Mývatn & Námaskarð
must_see.why: Otherworldly geothermal area with boiling mud pots, craters and a quieter blue lagoon alternative.

must_see.name: Landmannalaugar
must_see.why: Rainbow rhyolite mountains and hot-spring bathing at the Laugavegur trailhead (4x4/bus only).

must_see.name: Westfjords & Dynjandi
must_see.why: Iceland's least-visited region: a 100 m bridal-veil cascade and the Látrabjarg bird cliffs.

must_see.name: Húsavík
must_see.why: Europe's best whale watching, with humpbacks sighted on most summer tours.

must_see.name: Blue Lagoon or Sky Lagoon
must_see.why: Iconic geothermal spa bathing; Sky Lagoon is closer to town, local pools cost a tenth of the price.

insights: Extremely expensive: realistic budget travel runs ISK 13,000-31,000/day (~EUR 90-215); mid-range easily doubles that. Shop at Bónus or Krónan supermarkets and self-cater.
Essentially cashless, cards/phones work everywhere including remote fuel pumps (a PIN credit card is essential).
Alcohol is sold only in state Vínbúðin stores (limited hours); buy duty-free on arrival at Keflavík to save 30-50%.
Tap water is excellent and free everywhere, never buy bottled water.
Register travel plans and check conditions at safetravel.is; the 112 Iceland app can send your location to rescue services.
Midnight sun mid-May to end of July; northern lights visible roughly September-March.
Tipping is not expected anywhere, service is included.
The famous hot dog (pylsa, ~ISK 700/EUR 5) and bakery/soup deals are the cheapest hot meals.

Faroe Islands.best_time_note: June-August have the longest days, ferry/helicopter access to Mykines and 'least bad' weather, though fog and rain can strike any day.

rail.note: No railways; travel is by car, the excellent SSL bus/ferry network, and subsidised helicopter hops between islands.

bus.note: SSL runs cheap buses and ferries to most islands (Tórshavn city buses are free); a travel card covers buses and ferries.

driving.tolls: Subsea tunnels: Eysturoy and Sandoy tunnels DKK 175 (~EUR 23.50) one-way without subscription (DKK 75 with); Vágar and Norðoy tunnels ~DKK 100 (~EUR 13) round trip, only charged one direction. Rentals usually auto-bill tolls.
warnings: Several older mountain and village tunnels are single-lane with passing bays, oncoming traffic has priority in marked directions
Sheep wander onto roads everywhere; hitting one means paying the farmer
Sudden fog can cut visibility to metres; drive slowly on cliff-edge roads
Some famous hikes cross private land and charge fees, e.g. ~DKK 200 for Sørvágsvatn or Kallur; Mykines charges a summer landing fee
driving.car_recommended_for: Almost everything, the islands are made for a 3-5 day self-drive, and buses to trailheads are infrequent
driving.car_not_needed_in: Tórshavn itself, or if you base there and use SSL buses/ferries plus a couple of tours

must_see.name: Múlafossur waterfall, Gásadalur
must_see.why: The iconic waterfall dropping straight off a cliff into the ocean, 15 minutes from the airport.

must_see.name: Sørvágsvatn (lake above the ocean)
must_see.why: Optical-illusion lake hanging over the sea at Trælanípa cliff; ~3h round-trip hike, fee payable.

must_see.name: Kallur lighthouse, Kalsoy
must_see.why: Knife-edge ridge hike from Trollanes with the archipelago's best viewpoint (ferry from Klaksvík).

must_see.name: Mykines
must_see.why: Thousands of puffins line the path to the lighthouse (May-Aug); book the ferry well ahead.

must_see.name: Saksun
must_see.why: Amphitheatre village with a tidal lagoon and turf-roofed church at the end of a lonely valley.

must_see.name: Gjógv
must_see.why: Village named after its 200 m natural sea-filled gorge harbour, below Slættaratindur peak.

must_see.name: Tórshavn old town (Tinganes)
must_see.why: Turf-roofed government quarter of one of the world's smallest, cosiest capitals.

must_see.name: Viðareiði & Villingardalsfjall
must_see.why: Northernmost village beneath a hikeable peak with views over Cape Enniberg's 750 m sea cliff.

insights: Part of the Danish Kingdom but outside the EU and formally outside Schengen, carry a passport; there are no routine checks arriving from Denmark.
No Ryanair service: fly Atlantic Airways from Copenhagen (pair with a Denmark trip), Edinburgh or Billund, or take the Smyril Line ferry from Denmark.
Currency is the Faroese króna, 1:1 with Danish krone (DKK cards/notes work fine); cards accepted everywhere.
Weather changes hourly, never plan only one anchor activity per day, and check ferry/heli cancellations.
The subsidised Atlantic Airways helicopter between islands costs from ~EUR 20-30 but tourists may only book one direction in summer.
Alcohol is sold only in state Rúsdrekkasøla stores; supermarket beer is max 2.8%.
Hiking paths often cross private farmland, several now charge DKK 100-200; respect closures and take cash for honesty boxes.
Tipping is not expected; restaurants are few outside Tórshavn, so book dinner ahead.

Denmark.best_time_note: May-June and late August-September combine long daylight and mild weather with fewer crowds; July is peak Danish holiday season.

rail.note: DSB Orange advance fares (from ~DKK 99-149 Copenhagen-Aarhus) sell out fast; the Rejsekort/DSB app covers regional travel.

bus.note: Kombardo Expressen and FlixBus link Copenhagen with Aarhus/Aalborg from ~EUR 10-20, often undercutting trains.

driving.tolls: No road tolls except two bridges: Storebælt ~DKK 250 (~EUR 33) one-way for a car, and Øresund to Sweden DKK 470 (~EUR 63) standard one-way (big discounts with ØresundGO/online deals).
warnings: Always check bike lanes before turning right, cyclists have priority and are everywhere
Low-emission zones in Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg affect older diesel vehicles (mainly vans/trucks)
Speed cameras are common and fines are income-blind and steep
driving.car_recommended_for: Jutland's west coast, Skagen, Møns Klint, castles of Zealand and island-hopping to Funen
driving.car_not_needed_in: Copenhagen, bikes, metro and harbour buses beat a car, and parking is expensive

must_see.name: Nyhavn & central Copenhagen
must_see.why: The postcard canal plus Strøget, Christiansborg and the Little Mermaid within a walkable core.

must_see.name: Tivoli Gardens
must_see.why: The 1843 amusement park that inspired Disney, magical at dusk and at Christmas.

must_see.name: Kronborg Castle, Helsingør
must_see.why: Hamlet's Elsinore, a UNESCO Renaissance fortress guarding the Øresund strait.

must_see.name: Møns Klint
must_see.why: 128 m white chalk cliffs above turquoise water, Denmark's most dramatic nature.

must_see.name: Aarhus (ARoS & Den Gamle By)
must_see.why: Rainbow-panorama art museum and a walk-through open-air town spanning three centuries.

must_see.name: Skagen & Grenen
must_see.why: Stand where two seas visibly collide at Denmark's sandy northern tip, in famous painters' light.

must_see.name: Roskilde Viking Ship Museum
must_see.why: Five original Viking ships salvaged from the fjord, plus the royal tombs in the cathedral.

must_see.name: Ribe
must_see.why: Scandinavia's oldest town: crooked half-timbered lanes and Wadden Sea 'black sun' starling murmurations.

must_see.name: Legoland Billund
must_see.why: The original Legoland beside LEGO House in the brick's hometown.

must_see.name: Bornholm
must_see.why: Round churches, Hammershus castle ruin and smokehouses on a sunny Baltic outlier.

insights: Denmark is effectively cashless, some places no longer accept cash at all; contactless works everywhere.
Copenhagen Airport (CPH) is a Ryanair destination and the metro reaches the centre in 15 minutes; Billund and Aarhus are alternative Ryanair gateways.
Tipping is not expected, service is included by law; round up at most.
Rent a bike in Copenhagen: the city has more bikes than people and superb infrastructure.
Many Copenhagen highlights are free (Nyhavn, changing of the guard, Christiania, harbour swims); the Copenhagen Card pays off only on museum-heavy days.
Supermarket chains Netto, Rema 1000 and Lidl keep food costs down; bakeries sell cheap quality breakfasts.
Day-trip to Malmö/Lund in Sweden by train over the Øresund bridge (~35-40 min), bring your passport/ID for occasional Swedish border checks.

Norway.best_time_note: June-August for fjord hikes and midnight sun; late September-March for northern lights in Tromsø and Lofoten.

rail.note: Minipris advance fares from ~NOK 249-299 make the spectacular Oslo-Bergen line affordable; the Flåm Railway branch is a top scenic ride.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches fill rail gaps (e.g. to Ålesund, Lofoten); FlixBus Oslo routes are the cheapest intercity option.

driving.tolls: Extensive free-flow AutoPASS tolls: Oslo ring NOK 38-50 (~EUR 3.20-4.30) per pass for petrol cars in 2026, plus tunnel/road projects and fjord ferries; rental cars are auto-registered and tolls billed to your card.
warnings: Strict speed enforcement with average-speed cameras; fines are among the world's highest and the alcohol limit is 0.02%
Winter tyres required roughly Nov-Apr; many scenic mountain passes (e.g. Trollstigen) close October-May
Fjord routes rely on car ferries, check schedules; distances take far longer than maps suggest
Budget for tolls and ferries: a 1-2 week road trip can add EUR 100-200
driving.car_recommended_for: Lofoten, fjord Norway (Geiranger, Atlantic Ocean Road), Senja and anywhere beyond the rail network
driving.car_not_needed_in: Oslo and Bergen; the Oslo-Bergen train + Norway in a Nutshell covers classic fjords car-free

must_see.name: Lofoten Islands
must_see.why: Granite peaks straight out of the Arctic sea, red rorbuer cabins and beaches like Haukland.

must_see.name: Geirangerfjord
must_see.why: UNESCO fjord with the Seven Sisters falls, seen from the Eagle Road or a kayak.

must_see.name: Nærøyfjord & Flåm
must_see.why: The narrowest UNESCO fjord arm, linked by the famous Flåm mountain railway.

must_see.name: Bergen & Bryggen
must_see.why: Hanseatic wooden wharf, fish market and the Fløibanen funicular above seven mountains.

must_see.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
must_see.why: A 604 m flat-topped cliff over Lysefjord, reached by a moderate 8 km round-trip hike.

must_see.name: Trolltunga
must_see.why: The famous rock tongue over a lake, a demanding 27 km hike for fit, prepared hikers.

must_see.name: Tromsø
must_see.why: The northern-lights capital, with whale safaris and the Arctic Cathedral.

must_see.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
must_see.why: Eight bridges leaping between islets, one of the world's great short drives.

must_see.name: Oslo (Opera House, Vigeland, Munch)
must_see.why: Walk the opera roof, 200+ Vigeland sculptures free in Frogner Park, and The Scream.

must_see.name: Ålesund
must_see.why: Art-nouveau town rebuilt after the 1904 fire, with the Aksla viewpoint's 418 steps.

must_see.name: Senja
must_see.why: Lofoten-grade scenery (Segla peak, Tungeneset) without Lofoten's crowds.

insights: Allemannsretten (right to roam): you may hike and wild-camp on uncultivated land, at least 150 m from houses, for up to 2 nights per spot.
Alcohol above 4.7% is sold only at state Vinmonopolet shops (closed Sundays, early Saturday close); a beer in a bar runs EUR 9-13, so many pre-buy.
Nearly cashless, cards/Vipps everywhere; tipping is optional (round up or ~5-10% for great service).
Midnight sun roughly mid-May to late July and polar night Nov-Jan above the Arctic Circle (Tromsø, Lofoten).
Eating out is brutal on budgets: supermarkets (Kiwi, Rema 1000, Extra) plus bakery lunches and free tap water keep costs sane.
Ryanair serves Oslo Torp and Haugesund (not Gardermoen) from Belgium, Torp is ~1h45 by bus from Oslo; factor transfer cost/time.
Book minipris train and Hurtigruten/ferry legs weeks ahead in summer; Lofoten accommodation sells out by spring.

Sweden.best_time_note: June-August bring warm days, midsummer festivities and open archipelago boats; December-March is prime for Lapland aurora and snow.

rail.note: Book early for cheap fixed-price fares; SJ and Vy night trains run from Stockholm/Gothenburg to Swedish Lapland (Kiruna, Abisko).

bus.note: FlixBus blankets the south cheaply; Bus4You offers comfier intercity coaches on main corridors.

driving.tolls: Congestion taxes in Stockholm and Gothenburg are billed automatically by plate (up to ~SEK 45/pass at peak); bridge tolls at Motala, Sundsvall and the Øresund crossing to Denmark; rentals pass charges to you.
warnings: Moose and deer collisions are a real risk at dawn/dusk, especially in forested regions, heed wildlife fencing gaps
Winter tyres are mandatory 1 Dec-31 Mar in winter conditions
Drink-driving limit is 0.02% with heavy penalties
driving.car_recommended_for: Skane and Osterlen coast, Dalarna, High Coast, Oland/Gotland (with ferry) and Lapland road trips
driving.car_not_needed_in: Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö, transit and archipelago ferries cover the classics

must_see.name: Stockholm Gamla Stan & Vasa Museum
must_see.why: Medieval old town plus a fully preserved 1628 warship raised from the harbour.

must_see.name: Stockholm Archipelago
must_see.why: 30,000 islands reachable by Waxholmsbolaget ferries, Vaxholm and Grinda make easy day trips.

must_see.name: Visby, Gotland
must_see.why: A walled Hanseatic rose-covered town, UNESCO-listed and magical in summer.

must_see.name: Abisko National Park
must_see.why: Statistically among Europe's clearest aurora skies, plus the start of the Kungsleden trail.

must_see.name: Icehotel, Jukkasjärvi
must_see.why: The original hotel rebuilt from Torne river ice each winter (visitable by day).

must_see.name: Gothenburg & southern archipelago
must_see.why: Laid-back second city with car-free islands, Liseberg park and Sweden's best seafood.

must_see.name: Österlen & Ales Stenar
must_see.why: A megalithic stone ship on coastal cliffs amid orchards and art studios.

must_see.name: High Coast (Höga Kusten)
must_see.why: UNESCO coastline of red granite domes and the Skuleskogen sea-view hikes.

must_see.name: Dalarna (Lake Siljan & Falun)
must_see.why: The heartland of red cottages, Dala horses and a UNESCO copper mine.

must_see.name: Malmö & Lund
must_see.why: Turning Torso, canals and a 1000-year-old university town, 40 min from Copenhagen.

insights: The world's most cashless country, many cafes, buses and toilets refuse cash entirely; bring a contactless card and expect card-only signs ('Kontantfritt').
Alcohol above 3.5% is sold only at Systembolaget (closes ~15:00 Saturday, shut Sundays), plan weekend purchases ahead.
Allemansrätten (right of public access) lets you hike, forage berries/mushrooms and camp a night or two on most land, away from homes.
Fika (coffee + cinnamon bun break) is a daily institution; cafe fika deals are the cheap way to snack.
Midsummer (late June) is the real national holiday: cities empty, shops shut, and countryside celebrations welcome visitors.
Tipping is not expected; rounding up is plenty.
Ryanair uses Stockholm Arlanda plus Gothenburg Landvetter and Växjö/Malmö on some routes, check which airport before booking transfers.
Lunch 'dagens rätt' specials (~SEK 120-150 incl. salad/coffee) are the best-value restaurant meals.

Finland.best_time_note: June-August for lakes, archipelago and midnight sun; December-March for Lapland snow, huskies and northern lights (aurora season runs Aug-Apr).

rail.note: Advance saver fares are cheap (Helsinki-Tampere from ~EUR 10); the overnight Santa Claus Express to Rovaniemi has sleeper cabins and car carriages.

bus.note: OnniBus double-deckers offer intercity fares from a few euros; Matkahuolto aggregates the dense regional bus network.

driving.tolls: None, Finland has no road tolls, vignettes or congestion charges.
warnings: Reindeer roam roads freely in Lapland and moose are a hazard everywhere, collisions must be reported (112)
Winter tyres are mandatory roughly Nov-Mar; icy roads persist into April in the north
Distances are long and fuel stops sparse in the north, plan Lapland legs carefully
driving.car_recommended_for: Lakeland loops (Saimaa), Koli, the Turku archipelago trail and summer Lapland
driving.car_not_needed_in: Helsinki/Tampere/Turku, or winter Lapland packages where resorts run transfers

must_see.name: Helsinki & Suomenlinna
must_see.why: Design-district capital with a UNESCO sea fortress a 15-minute city ferry away.

must_see.name: Rovaniemi & Santa Claus Village
must_see.why: Meet Santa on the Arctic Circle year-round, with husky and reindeer farms nearby.

must_see.name: Lake Saimaa & Savonlinna
must_see.why: Medieval Olavinlinna castle on an island in Europe's fourth-largest lake, home to rare ringed seals.

must_see.name: Koli National Park
must_see.why: The national-romantic view over Lake Pielinen that inspired Sibelius and Finnish painters.

must_see.name: Nuuksio National Park
must_see.why: Wilderness lakes and boardwalk trails only 45 minutes from the capital.

must_see.name: Tampere
must_see.why: The 'sauna capital of the world', try the 1906 Rajaportti public sauna between two lakes.

must_see.name: Turku & Archipelago Trail
must_see.why: Finland's oldest city and a 250 km bikeable ring of bridges and small ferries through 20,000 islands.

must_see.name: Åland Islands
must_see.why: Swedish-speaking island world of red granite, cycling routes and Kastelholm castle.

must_see.name: Inari & Sámi culture
must_see.why: The Siida museum and Lake Inari offer the deepest introduction to indigenous Sámi life.

must_see.name: Ylläs & Pallas-Yllästunturi NP
must_see.why: Finland's cleanest air, seven fells and superb aurora viewing away from resort light.

insights: Sauna is the national institution (~3 million saunas): try a public one like Löyly (Helsinki) or Rajaportti (Tampere); nudity is normal, swimwear rules vary by venue.
Jokamiehenoikeus (everyman's rights) allows hiking, berry/mushroom foraging and short-term camping on almost all land.
Alcohol above 8% is sold only at state Alko stores (grocery stores now sell up to 8%); Alko closes early Saturday, shut Sundays.
Finland uses the euro (only Nordic country that does) and is essentially cashless, cards everywhere.
Midnight sun in Lapland from June to mid-July; polar night (kaamos) in December; aurora visible roughly late August-April.
Tipping is not expected, service is always included.
Ryanair flies from Belgium to Helsinki (and seasonally Lapland via other carriers); OnniBus + VR savers make domestic hops cheap.
Tap water is among the world's cleanest; lunch buffets (~EUR 11-14) are the budget way to eat out.

Greece.best_time_note: May-June and September-October give warm seas without July-August heatwaves, crowds and peak ferry prices.

rail.note: Rail is limited to the Athens-Thessaloniki spine plus a few branches; for the Peloponnese, Epirus and all islands, KTEL buses and ferries beat trains.

bus.note: Regional KTEL cooperatives cover almost every town cheaply; for islands book ferries on Ferryhopper (ferryhopper.com), well ahead in August.

driving.tolls: Per-gate motorway tolls (roughly EUR 2-4 per gate) on A1, A2 Egnatia, Attiki Odos and Rio-Antirrio bridge; a long drive adds up fast.
warnings: Avoid quad-bike/ATV rentals on islands: frequent serious accidents and insurance often invalid without the right licence
Mountain and island roads are narrow with blind bends and goats; locals overtake aggressively
Athens centre has a residents' ring restriction (daktylios) and hopeless parking - skip driving there
driving.car_recommended_for: Crete's interior, the Mani and inner Peloponnese, Zagori villages, and larger islands like Naxos or Lesbos
driving.car_not_needed_in: Athens, Thessaloniki, Santorini/Mykonos cores, and small islands with bus networks

must_see.name: Acropolis of Athens
must_see.why: The Parthenon at dawn or last slot is still the defining Greek sight - now timed-entry with a 20,000/day cap.

must_see.name: Meteora
must_see.why: Monasteries perched on sandstone pillars, reachable by train from Athens to Kalambaka.

must_see.name: Zagori & Vikos Gorge
must_see.why: Stone villages, arched bridges and one of the world's deepest gorges, almost tourist-free.

must_see.name: Mani Peninsula
must_see.why: Tower-house villages, wild coast and sea caves at the Peloponnese's rugged southern tip.

must_see.name: Nafplio & Epidaurus
must_see.why: Greece's prettiest seaside town pairs with the ancient theatre's summer performances.

must_see.name: Delphi
must_see.why: The ancient oracle's sanctuary hangs dramatically on the slopes of Mount Parnassus.

must_see.name: Naxos
must_see.why: Big beaches, mountain villages and half the price of neighbouring Santorini and Mykonos.

must_see.name: Milos
must_see.why: Lunar volcanic coastline (Sarakiniko) and boat trips to Kleftiko rock formations.

must_see.name: Chania & Samaria Gorge
must_see.why: Venetian harbour town plus Europe's classic 16 km gorge hike (open roughly May-Oct).

must_see.name: Thessaloniki
must_see.why: Byzantine churches, great food scene and nightlife at northern-Greece prices.

must_see.name: Monemvasia
must_see.why: A medieval walled town hidden on the seaward side of a giant rock, car-free inside.

insights: Acropolis tickets are EUR 30 with mandatory 2-hour timed slots and a 20,000/day cap - book on the official hhticket.gr a few days ahead in summer
Book August ferries weeks in advance (Ferryhopper); strikes occasionally cancel sailings, so avoid same-day ferry-to-flight connections
July-August heatwaves regularly top 40C; archaeological sites may close midday during extreme heat - go at opening time
Tap water is not drinkable on many Cyclades and Dodecanese islands (fine in Athens, Thessaloniki, Crete) - ask locally
Monasteries (Meteora, Athos area) enforce dress codes: covered shoulders, long skirts/trousers; wraps are lent at Meteora
In Athens taxis insist on the meter (tariff 1 daytime); at the airport use the fixed EUR 40 flat fare to the centre, or take the metro
Plumbing is narrow almost everywhere: toilet paper goes in the bin, not the bowl
Cards are accepted nearly everywhere now, but small tavernas and kiosks still prefer cash

Cyprus.best_time_note: April-May and October-November are warm and uncrowded, and the sea stays swimmable into November; July-August is brutally hot.

rail.note: Cyprus has NO railway at all; intercity buses or a rental car are the only ways to get around.

bus.note: Intercity buses link the main cities for about EUR 4-7, but they thin out on Sundays and barely serve Troodos or Akamas.

warnings: Cyprus drives on the LEFT (UK-style) - rental cars are right-hand-drive with distinctive red plates
Crossing into Northern Cyprus by car requires separate insurance bought at the checkpoint (roughly EUR 25-40/month)
Skip quad-bike and buggy rentals around Ayia Napa - accident rates are high and cover is poor
Troodos roads are winding and can get snow and ice December-February
driving.car_recommended_for: Troodos mountains and painted churches, Akamas Peninsula, wine villages, and hopping between remote beaches
driving.car_not_needed_in: Larnaca, Limassol and Nicosia centres, or a stay based in one resort town

must_see.name: Nicosia old town & Green Line
must_see.why: Europe's last divided capital - walk through the Ledra Street checkpoint between two worlds.

must_see.name: Troodos painted churches
must_see.why: Ten UNESCO-listed Byzantine churches with vivid frescoes hidden in mountain villages.

must_see.name: Kykkos Monastery
must_see.why: Cyprus's richest monastery, glittering with mosaics deep in the mountains.

must_see.name: Paphos Archaeological Park
must_see.why: Spectacular Roman floor mosaics and the Tombs of the Kings by the harbour.

must_see.name: Akamas Peninsula & Blue Lagoon
must_see.why: Undeveloped cape with the Aphrodite trail, gorges and turquoise coves.

must_see.name: Cape Greco
must_see.why: Sea caves and cliff walks between Ayia Napa and Protaras, best at sunrise.

must_see.name: Petra tou Romiou (Aphrodite's Rock)
must_see.why: The mythic birthplace of Aphrodite on a dramatic pebble beach.

must_see.name: Omodos & Krasochoria wine villages
must_see.why: Cobbled lanes and family wineries pouring Commandaria and Xynisteri.

must_see.name: Kyrenia (Girne)
must_see.why: A horseshoe harbour under a crusader castle, the north's prettiest town.

must_see.name: Salamis ruins & Famagusta
must_see.why: Vast Roman ruins plus the ghost resort of Varosha, partially reopened to visitors.

insights: You can cross the Green Line with a passport/EU ID at checkpoints like Ledra Street, but arriving on the island via Ercan (north) airport counts as illegal entry to the Republic - fly into Larnaca or Paphos
Northern Cyprus uses Turkish lira, though euros are widely accepted at poor rates; get some lira for buses and small shops
There is no Uber - use Bolt or agree taxi fares upfront; taxis are expensive by local standards
Buses run reduced or no service on Sundays and holidays - plan Troodos or Akamas trips around it
Tap water is safe but heavily mineral; most locals drink bottled
July-August regularly hits 35-40C inland at Nicosia - base yourself on the coast or in Troodos
Sunbeds, boat trips and meze feasts add up: Cyprus runs noticeably pricier than Greece's islands for eating out

Bulgaria.best_time_note: May-June and September are ideal for cities and mountains; July works for high Rila/Pirin hikes, and January-March is bargain skiing in Bansko.

rail.note: Trains are very cheap but slow and dated; buses are usually faster between Sofia, Plovdiv, Veliko Tarnovo and the coast - the scenic exception is the narrow-gauge Septemvri-Dobrinishte line.

bus.note: Intercity buses are the workhorse of Bulgarian travel; compare schedules on bgrazpisanie.com and buy at the station or online.

driving.vignette: E-vignette required on national roads/motorways: weekend EUR 5.11, weekly EUR 7.67, monthly EUR 15.34, annual EUR 49.60; buy at bgtoll.bg (a EUR 4.09 one-day vignette exists since Feb 2026)
driving.tolls: The vignette covers cars fully; distance-based tolling applies only to trucks and buses
warnings: Aggressive overtaking and high accident rates - drive defensively, especially on the Sofia-Plovdiv and coastal roads
Secondary roads can be potholed and unlit; watch for stray dogs and horse carts in rural areas
Buy the e-vignette BEFORE entering a motorway - cameras enforce instantly and fines follow rental cars home
driving.car_recommended_for: Rila and Rhodope backroads, monastery loops, Buzludzha, Belogradchik and village guesthouses
driving.car_not_needed_in: Sofia, Plovdiv, Veliko Tarnovo and Bansko, all reachable by bus or train

must_see.name: Rila Monastery
must_see.why: Bulgaria's iconic striped monastery in a forested valley - combine with a Rila backcountry hike or overnight in the monastery itself.

must_see.name: Seven Rila Lakes
must_see.why: A chairlift-assisted alpine cirque hike over glacial lakes, best July-September.

must_see.name: Plovdiv Old Town & Kapana
must_see.why: Roman theatre, Revival-era houses and the Kapana creative quarter in Europe's oldest continuously inhabited city.

must_see.name: Veliko Tarnovo & Tsarevets
must_see.why: The medieval capital stacked above a river gorge, with a summer sound-and-light show on the fortress.

must_see.name: Rhodope villages (Shiroka Laka, Trigrad)
must_see.why: Bagpipe country: stone villages, the Trigrad Gorge and Devil's Throat cave.

must_see.name: Buzludzha Monument
must_see.why: The abandoned UFO-shaped communist congress hall on a mountaintop - a cult photo stop (interior closed).

must_see.name: Belogradchik Rocks & Fortress
must_see.why: Red sandstone towers wrapped around an Ottoman fortress, far off the tourist trail.

must_see.name: Sozopol & Nessebar
must_see.why: Two wooden-house peninsula old towns; go June or September to dodge resort crowds.

must_see.name: Koprivshtitsa
must_see.why: A perfectly preserved National Revival village of colourful mansions.

must_see.name: Sofia's Alexander Nevsky & Vitosha
must_see.why: Gold-domed cathedral plus a 2,290 m mountain on the city's doorstep.

insights: Bulgaria switched from the lev to the EURO on 1 January 2026 (fixed at 1.95583 BGN = 1 EUR); since 1 February 2026 the euro is the only legal cash - refuse any change given in leva
It is now the cheapest eurozone country: expect EUR 2-3 draft beer and hearty mains under EUR 8 outside Sofia's centre
Head gestures are reversed: a nod can mean 'no' and a head shake 'yes' - confirm verbally
Signage is in Cyrillic; learning the alphabet pays off hugely on buses and menus
Cards work fine in cities but carry some cash for villages, monasteries and mountain huts
Stray dogs are common in rural areas and suburbs - give them space
Monasteries expect covered shoulders and knees; Rila offers basic overnight cells for early photos before tour buses arrive
events: Surva Kukeri masquerade festival, Pernik (late January)
Kapana Fest, Plovdiv (several editions per year)

Romania.best_time_note: May-June and September are best for cities and Transylvania; July-early October is the only window for the Transfagarasan and high Carpathian hikes.

rail.note: The network is extensive and scenic (Brasov-Sighisoara, Oravita-Anina) but slow - buses or BlaBlaCar often halve journey times on busy corridors.

bus.note: Autogari.ro aggregates hundreds of minibus and coach operators; it is the practical way to reach Maramures and rural Transylvania.

driving.vignette: Rovinieta e-vignette required on all national roads/motorways: about EUR 3.50 for 1 day, EUR 6 for 10 days, EUR 9.50 for 30 days (roviniete.ro or petrol stations)
driving.tolls: Separate small tolls for the A2 Fetesti Danube bridge and the Giurgiu-Ruse bridge to Bulgaria
warnings: Transfagarasan (DN7C) and Transalpina high sections are open roughly July-October only - check before planning a trip around them
Expect horse carts, slow trucks and risky overtaking on single-carriageway national roads; night driving is best avoided
Brown bears beg along the Transfagarasan - never feed them or leave the car close by
driving.car_recommended_for: Saxon villages (Viscri, Biertan), Maramures, Bucovina's painted monasteries, and the Transfagarasan/Transalpina
driving.car_not_needed_in: Bucharest, Brasov, Cluj and Sibiu, which connect fine by train or bus

must_see.name: Transfagarasan Highway
must_see.why: A hairpin spectacle over a 2,042 m pass past Balea Lake - drive it early morning, July-October.

must_see.name: Painted monasteries of Bucovina
must_see.why: Voronet, Sucevita and Moldovita wear 500-year-old exterior frescoes in UNESCO-listed blue and gold.

must_see.name: Maramures wooden churches & Merry Cemetery
must_see.why: Living folk culture: towering wooden steeples and Sapanta's witty painted grave markers.

must_see.name: Sighisoara
must_see.why: An inhabited medieval citadel and Vlad the Impaler's birthplace.

must_see.name: Brasov & Bran Castle
must_see.why: Gothic old town under Mount Tampa, with the 'Dracula's castle' crowd-pleaser nearby.

must_see.name: Viscri & Biertan fortified churches
must_see.why: Saxon village Romania at its most timeless, minus Bran's crowds.

must_see.name: Peles Castle
must_see.why: The Hohenzollern royal retreat is one of Europe's most opulent 19th-century castles.

must_see.name: Sibiu
must_see.why: Elegant squares, the 'eyes' rooftops and a top-tier food scene.

must_see.name: Danube Delta
must_see.why: Europe's greatest wetland - boat out of Tulcea to fishing villages and pelican colonies (May-September).

must_see.name: Turda Salt Mine
must_see.why: A surreal underground amusement hall with a boating lake 120 m down.

must_see.name: Corvin Castle
must_see.why: Romania's most dramatic Gothic castle, drawbridge and all.

must_see.name: Bucharest Old Town & Palace of Parliament
must_see.why: Belle-epoque remnants and Ceausescu's megalomaniac palace, the world's heaviest building.

insights: Romania still uses the leu (RON), not the euro - cards are accepted almost everywhere, but keep small cash for markets, rural guesthouses and church donations
Avoid touting taxis at Bucharest's airport and Gara de Nord - Bolt and Uber are cheap, ubiquitous and scam-free
Buy the rovinieta before leaving the rental lot or border; camera enforcement is automatic and fines chase rental cars
Trains are safe but slow - for Bucharest-Brasov take the train, elsewhere check Autogari.ro buses first
Bears are a real hazard in the Carpathians: keep food sealed when hiking and heed local warnings
Monasteries in Bucovina and elsewhere expect covered knees/shoulders; wraps are usually provided at the gate
Tap water is safe in cities; stray dogs are far fewer than their old reputation but still appear on rural edges
Summer festival weeks (Untold, Electric Castle) spike Cluj accommodation prices - book months ahead or stay outside town

Moldova.best_time_note: Late spring and the September-October grape harvest are ideal - early October brings Wine Day, the country's biggest party.

rail.note: Rail is minimal and slow - beyond the Chisinau-Iasi/Bucharest 'Prietenia' sleeper, buses and marshrutkas beat trains on every route.

operators: Marshrutka/minibus networks from Chisinau's Gara Centrala, Nord and Sud
bus.note: Frequent, dirt-cheap marshrutkas (pay the driver in MDL) reach every town, plus international coaches to Iasi, Bucharest and Odesa.

driving.vignette: Foreign-registered cars must buy an e-vignette for national (M/R) roads - about EUR 4-5 for 7 days, online (evignieta) or at MAIB bank branches; the fine is ~EUR 52
warnings: Do not enter Moldova through Transnistria from the Ukrainian side - you get no Moldovan entry stamp and problems on exit
Rural roads are potholed and unlit; avoid night driving and watch for carts and animals
Police checkpoints are routine - carry documents and keep headlights on where required
driving.car_recommended_for: Winery-hopping (Cricova, Castel Mimi, Purcari), Orheiul Vechi and Soroca in one flexible loop
driving.car_not_needed_in: Chisinau, and Cricova/Milestii Mici tours are reachable by taxi or organised transfer

must_see.name: Cricova winery
must_see.why: A 120 km underground wine city you tour by electric car - book tastings several days ahead.

must_see.name: Milestii Mici
must_see.why: The world's largest wine cellar by Guinness record, holding some 1.5 million bottles underground.

must_see.name: Orheiul Vechi
must_see.why: A cave monastery carved into a limestone ridge above a looping river - Moldova's signature landscape.

must_see.name: Soroca Fortress & Gypsy Hill
must_see.why: A perfectly round medieval Dniester fortress beside the flamboyant mansions of the Roma quarter.

must_see.name: Tiraspol & Bender fortress (Transnistria)
must_see.why: A day trip into a Soviet time capsule with its own border, currency and Lenin statues.

must_see.name: Chisinau markets & parks
must_see.why: The Central Market, Stefan cel Mare park and brutalist-era architecture reward a slow day with wine bars.

insights: Currency is the Moldovan leu (MDL); cards work in Chisinau but carry cash for marshrutkas, markets and everything rural
Transnistria runs its own 'border': bring your passport, keep the entry slip, and register if staying overnight; only its own ruble is accepted - change a little on arrival
Wine is the reason to come - Cricova and Milestii Mici require advance booking, and tastings with lunch cost a fraction of Western Europe
Moldova is arguably Europe's cheapest country: good mains for EUR 4-6 and decent doubles under EUR 40 in the capital
Stick to bottled or filtered water outside Chisinau
Romanian is official but Russian is widely understood; a few words of either go a long way as English is patchy outside the capital
There are no Ryanair routes to Chisinau - budget flyers typically connect via Iasi (Romania) and take the 3-4 h bus or Prietenia train across
food: Mamaliga with brinza and sour cream
Feteasca Neagra wine and divin brandy
events: National Wine Day, Chisinau (first weekend of October)

France.best_time_note: May-June and September-October give warm weather without August crowds; most of France (and Paris) empties in August when locals holiday, but the coasts are packed.

rail.note: Book TGVs 2-3 months ahead; low-cost Ouigo TGVs start around €10-19 (Paris-Lyon/Bordeaux/Marseille) but have luggage limits. TER regional trains are fixed-price, no booking needed.

bus.note: Intercity buses are far cheaper than walk-up train fares; Paris-Lyon often under €15.

driving.tolls: Extensive autoroute tolls, among Europe's priciest: Paris-Nice ~€80, Paris-Bordeaux ~€60. Free routes nationales are slower but scenic.
warnings: Crit'Air sticker (~€3.85 via certificat-air.gouv.fr, order weeks ahead) required in 40+ low-emission zones incl. Paris, Lyon, Marseille, €68 fine without it
Priorite a droite: traffic from the right has priority at many unmarked junctions
Speed limit 80 km/h on most undivided rural roads; heavy automated camera enforcement
Fuel on autoroutes costs ~€0.20-0.30/L more, fill up at supermarket stations
driving.car_recommended_for: Dordogne, Loire chateaux, Provence hill villages, Normandy D-Day coast, Alsace wine route, Verdon Gorge
driving.car_not_needed_in: Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Nice, Bordeaux, Strasbourg

must_see.name: Paris (Louvre & Montmartre)
must_see.why: The world's most-visited city still earns it, but book Louvre and Eiffel Tower timed slots weeks ahead.

must_see.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
must_see.why: Tidal island abbey that looks conjured from a fantasy novel; stay nearby to see it floodlit after day-trippers leave.

must_see.name: Gorges du Verdon
must_see.why: Europe's deepest turquoise canyon, kayak under 700 m limestone cliffs for a fraction of Riviera prices.

must_see.name: Colmar & the Alsace wine route
must_see.why: Half-timbered villages (Riquewihr, Eguisheim) among Grand Cru vineyards, with a Germanic food culture unique in France.

must_see.name: Dordogne valley
must_see.why: Prehistoric cave art (Lascaux IV), clifftop castles and Sarlat's medieval market, France's best-value gourmet region.

must_see.name: Etretat cliffs
must_see.why: The white chalk arches Monet painted, an easy cheap coastal escape from Paris via Le Havre.

must_see.name: Carcassonne
must_see.why: A complete double-walled medieval citadel; sleep inside the walls to have it to yourself at dawn.

must_see.name: Annecy
must_see.why: Canals, turquoise alpine lake you can swim in, and a cycling path circling it, the Alps without ski-resort prices in summer.

must_see.name: Corsica (Calanques de Piana & GR20)
must_see.why: Red granite fjords and Europe's most famous mountain trek; feels like a different country because it half is.

must_see.name: Camargue
must_see.why: Wild white horses, pink flamingos and rice marshes in the Rhone delta, bizarre, beautiful and free to explore by bike.

insights: Paris tourist tax rose again Jan 2026: ~€5.53/night in 3-star hotels up to €15.93 in palaces and unclassified rentals, per person
Major museums (Louvre, Orsay) require timed online tickets; many national museums are free the 1st Sunday of the month
Strikes (greves) regularly hit SNCF and air traffic control, check the day before travel and avoid tight connections
Pickpockets and the 'gold ring' / petition scams cluster around Montmartre, Eiffel Tower and metro line 1
Lunch is the budget hack: the same restaurant's midday prix-fixe menu often costs half the dinner price
Tap water is safe and free, ask for 'une carafe d'eau' with meals
Outside big cities almost everything closes Sunday and often Monday; plan food shopping around it
Cards are accepted nearly everywhere, but some bakeries and markets set a €5-10 card minimum
food: Fresh croissants and baguette tradition from an artisan boulangerie
Cheese + natural wine bars (comptoirs) for cheap gourmet dinners

Spain.best_time_note: April-June and September-October are ideal; inland Andalusia regularly tops 40C in July-August while the north coast stays mild all summer.

rail.note: High-speed competition means Madrid-Barcelona/Valencia/Seville from €7-20 on Avlo, Ouigo and iryo if booked 1-2 months ahead. Compare all three operators; walk-up AVE fares are steep.

bus.note: ALSA's dense network is often the only public transport to white villages and national parks.

driving.tolls: Cheaper than France: many autopistas went toll-free since 2021 (AP-7, AP-2, AP-4); tolls remain on AP-6, AP-9 (Galicia), AP-66 and a few others.
warnings: Madrid and Barcelona ZBE low-emission zones: foreign cars must register in advance or risk €200 fines
Theft from parked rental cars is common at beach and trailhead car parks, leave nothing visible
Balearics approved a new levy on non-local/rental vehicles (up to ~€85 by stay length/emissions), check before island road trips
Radar enforcement is heavy; fines reach foreign drivers via EU plate exchange
driving.car_recommended_for: Andalusian white villages, Picos de Europa, Galicia's coast, Extremadura, inland Aragon
driving.car_not_needed_in: Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Valencia, Bilbao, San Sebastian

must_see.name: Alhambra
must_see.why: The Nasrid Palaces are Europe's finest Moorish architecture, but tickets sell out weeks ahead on the official site.

must_see.name: Sagrada Familia & Gaudi's Barcelona
must_see.why: Gaudi's basilica nears completion for its 2026 centenary year; book timed entry 2-4 weeks out.

must_see.name: Mezquita of Cordoba
must_see.why: A cathedral inside a 1,000-pillar mosque; go at 8:30 for the free early-entry hour (Mon-Sat).

must_see.name: San Sebastian & Basque coast
must_see.why: The world's best casual food city, pintxo-bar hopping in the Parte Vieja beats any Michelin tasting menu for value.

must_see.name: Picos de Europa
must_see.why: Jagged 2,600 m peaks 20 km from the sea, with cider houses and blue cheese caves in the valleys, Spain's wildest cheap escape.

must_see.name: Ronda & the pueblos blancos
must_see.why: Whitewashed villages (Grazalema, Zahara, Setenil) strung across sierra roads, Spain's classic road trip.

must_see.name: Cies Islands
must_see.why: A Caribbean-looking Atlantic archipelago with a strict daily visitor cap, get the free Xunta permit before the boat ticket.

must_see.name: Albarracin
must_see.why: Arguably Spain's most beautiful village, a pink medieval town few foreigners reach.

must_see.name: Cabo de Gata
must_see.why: Mainland Spain's last undeveloped coast: volcanic coves, no high-rises, and off-season solitude.

must_see.name: Toledo
must_see.why: Christian, Muslim and Jewish monuments on one hilltop, 33 minutes from Madrid by train, stay overnight for the lit-up old town.

insights: Catalonia doubled its tourist tax from 1 Apr 2026: Barcelona now €6-12 per person/night depending on category (first 7 nights); Balearics still €1-4/night with a peak-season rise debated
Book Alhambra (tickets.alhambra-patronato.es) and Sagrada Familia weeks ahead, both sell out in high season
Dinner starts ~21:00; most kitchens close 16:00-20:00, tapas bars and menu del dia (€12-16 lunch) bridge the gap
Small-town shops genuinely close ~14:00-17:00 for siesta; plan fuel and food stops accordingly
Pickpocketing on Las Ramblas, Barcelona metro and Madrid's Rastro market is endemic, front pockets only
Card payment is universal, even for a €1.50 coffee; you barely need cash
Regional trains and buses on holidays (Semana Santa, Aug 15) sell out, book like a flight
Free tap water must be provided in restaurants by law since 2022, just ask for 'agua del grifo'
food: Tortilla de patatas + vermut on tap
events: San Fermin bull running, Pamplona (6-14 July)
La Tomatina, Bunol (last Wednesday of August)

Portugal.best_time_note: Spring and early autumn are perfect countrywide; the Algarve triples in price in August, while Lisbon and Porto are pleasant (if breezy) even in winter.

rail.note: Lisbon-Porto Alfa Pendular/Intercidades promo fares start ~€10-15 when booked up to 2 months ahead on cp.pt. Scenic Douro line (Regua-Pocinho) is a fixed-price regional gem.

bus.note: Buses beat trains to the Algarve interior, Alentejo and anywhere trains don't reach.

driving.tolls: Since 1 Jan 2025 the ex-SCUT motorways (A22 Algarve, A23, A24, A25, A28 stretches) are toll-FREE. Remaining tolled motorways (A1, A2...) use booths/Via Verde; some sections are electronic-only.
warnings: Electronic-only toll gantries remain on some roads: foreign-plated cars should register a card at EASYToll machines near the border or get a rental transponder
Do not drive up to Sintra's palaces, roads gridlock and parking is near-impossible; take the train from Lisbon Rossio
Rural N-roads are twisty and slow; Portugal has one of Western Europe's higher road-fatality rates
Historic town centres have very narrow cobbled lanes, park outside the walls
driving.car_recommended_for: Alentejo, Douro Valley wine estates, Costa Vicentina, schist villages of central Portugal, Peneda-Geres
driving.car_not_needed_in: Lisbon, Porto, Sintra, Coimbra, Faro and the Algarve rail corridor

must_see.name: Lisbon's Alfama & miradouros
must_see.why: Fado drifting through tiled lanes and free sunset viewpoints, Europe's best-value capital experience.

must_see.name: Sintra (Pena Palace & Quinta da Regaleira)
must_see.why: Romantic-era palaces in misty forest; book timed Pena tickets online and go before 9:30 to dodge the crush.

must_see.name: Porto & Vila Nova de Gaia
must_see.why: Port-wine lodges, the azulejo-clad Sao Bento station and Europe's prettiest riverfront, all walkable.

must_see.name: Douro Valley
must_see.why: Terraced vineyards best seen from the €15 regional train hugging the river, one of Europe's great rail rides.

must_see.name: Alentejo (Evora & Monsaraz)
must_see.why: Roman temples, a bone chapel, hilltop whitewashed villages and €5 jugs of wine, Portugal at half Algarve prices.

must_see.name: Costa Vicentina
must_see.why: Wild surf beaches and the Fishermen's Trail, the undeveloped coast the southern Algarve lost.

must_see.name: Benagil caves & Seven Hanging Valleys
must_see.why: The famous sea-cave dome plus a clifftop trail linking the region's best coves; kayak in early morning.

must_see.name: Peneda-Geres National Park
must_see.why: Portugal's only national park: granite peaks, wild garrano ponies, Roman roads and swimming lagoons.

must_see.name: Nazare
must_see.why: Winter (Oct-Mar) brings 20 m+ monster waves watched from the fort, a free natural spectacle.

must_see.name: Piodao & the schist villages
must_see.why: Slate-built mountain hamlets in the Serra do Acor that most tourists never hear of.

insights: Lisbon's tourist tax is €4 per person/night (capped at 7 nights, under-13s exempt); Porto charges €3; many Algarve towns €1.50-2
The bread/olives 'couvert' brought unasked isn't free, send it back if you don't want it (no offence taken)
Atlantic water is cold (16-19C) even in August, with strong rips, swim at flagged beaches
Pickpockets work Lisbon's tram 28 and Cais do Sodre; the tram experience is identical on quieter route 12
Eat where locals do: tascas and pastelarias serve €8-10 daily plates (prato do dia)
Ryanair serves Porto, Lisbon and Faro from Belgium (Charleroi), making multi-city open-jaw trips cheap
Tipping is not expected, rounding up is plenty
Book Sintra, Belem Tower and Livraria Lello (Porto) tickets online; walk-up queues waste half a day
food: Pastel de nata (Manteigaria or Pasteis de Belem)

Italy.best_time_note: May-June and September-October offer the best weather-to-crowd ratio; August means 35C+ heat, packed coasts and shuttered city restaurants around Ferragosto.

rail.note: Frecciarossa/Italo Super Economy fares (Rome-Florence from ~€10-20) open ~4 months out and sell fast. Regional trains are fixed-price, never book ahead, just remember to validate paper tickets.

bus.note: Overnight FlixBus/Itabus routes to the south (Rome-Puglia/Sicily) undercut trains massively.

driving.tolls: Autostrade are tolled (~€7/100 km; Milan-Rome ~€45). Superstrade (SS roads) are free but slower.
warnings: ZTL camera zones in nearly every historic centre, one wrong turn = €80-100 fine per pass, mailed months later to your rental company
Milan's Area C congestion charge (€7.50) and Area B apply on weekdays
Southern city driving (Naples, Palermo) is genuinely chaotic; park outside and use transit
Fuel 'servito' lanes cost ~€0.20/L more than 'fai da te' self-service
driving.car_recommended_for: Tuscany's Val d'Orcia, Dolomites, Puglia, inland Sicily, Umbria
driving.car_not_needed_in: Rome, Milan, Florence, Venice, Naples, Cinque Terre, Amalfi Coast (use ferries/SITA bus)

must_see.name: Rome
must_see.why: The Pantheon (€5), Colosseum and now ticketed Trevi basin (€2), book Colosseum/Vatican slots weeks ahead.

must_see.name: Venice
must_see.why: Still worth it: sleep in the city (day-tripper fee then doesn't apply) and walk Cannaregio and Castello at dawn.

must_see.name: Dolomites (Alpe di Siusi, Tre Cime)
must_see.why: Europe's most dramatic mountains with excellent buses and rifugio lunches, hiking here is cheap once you arrive.

must_see.name: Val d'Orcia & Siena
must_see.why: The cypress-lined postcard Tuscany, best from an agriturismo between Pienza and Montalcino.

must_see.name: Matera
must_see.why: Cave dwellings inhabited for 9,000 years, now Italy's most atmospheric budget overnight stay.

must_see.name: Puglia (Alberobello, Ostuni, Salento)
must_see.why: Trulli houses, white hill towns and Italy's clearest swimming water at northern-Europe-beating prices; fly into Bari/Brindisi.

must_see.name: Ortigia & southeast Sicily
must_see.why: Baroque Noto and Ortigia's Greek-island feel, plus Etna, Sicily is Italy's best value region.

must_see.name: Cinque Terre
must_see.why: Five villages linked by cliff paths and a €5 train; visit May or October, and note popular trails now have a fee/booking system in peak season.

must_see.name: Bologna
must_see.why: Italy's food capital with almost no tourist premium, day-trip by train to Modena and Parma.

must_see.name: Procida & the Phlegraean coast
must_see.why: The pastel island Capri crowds skip, 40 minutes from Naples for a few euros by ferry.

must_see.name: Lake Como
must_see.why: Villa gardens and ferry-hopping between Bellagio and Varenna, do it as a cheap day trip from Milan.

insights: Venice charges day-trippers (14+) an access fee on 60 peak dates from 3 Apr to 26 Jul 2026, 08:30-16:00: €5 if booked 4+ days ahead, €10 last-minute (cda.veneziaunica.it); overnight guests are exempt but pay hotel tax
Rome's Trevi Fountain basin costs €2 (since 2 Feb 2026, 09:00-22:00); city taxes: Rome €4-10/night, Venice €1-5, Florence up to €8, always per person, in cash or card at checkout
Validate regional train tickets in the green machines before boarding, €50+ fine otherwise (app tickets are exempt)
'Coperto' (€1-3/person) and bread charges are legal and universal; sitting at a table can double your espresso price vs standing at the bar
Book ahead or miss out: Colosseum, Vatican Museums, Uffizi, Last Supper (Milan, releases months early), Borghese Gallery
Watch for taxi overcharging in Rome/Naples, use official ranks and the fixed airport fares (Rome FCO-centre €55)
Many restaurants close between lunch and 19:30, and much of Italy shuts around 15 Aug (Ferragosto)
Free water fountains (nasoni in Rome) are everywhere, carry a bottle
food: Pizza napoletana in Naples (€5-8 for the world's best)
Cacio e pepe / carbonara in Rome
events: Palio di Siena horse race (2 July & 16 August)

Andorra.best_time_note: December-March for some of Europe's cheapest big-area skiing (Grandvalira/Pal-Arinsal); June-September for high-Pyrenees hiking with empty trails.

rail.note: No trains in Andorra. Nearest stations: L'Hospitalet-pres-l'Andorre (France, connecting bus) and Lleida (Spain); most visitors come by direct bus instead.

bus.note: Direct coaches from Barcelona city/airport and Toulouse airport (~3h, €35-40 one-way) are the standard way in.

driving.tolls: No road tolls in Andorra itself; the Envalira Tunnel toward France charges ~€7-8 (the free pass over the 2,408 m Port d'Envalira is spectacular in summer).
warnings: Winter equipment (chains or winter tyres) legally required in snow conditions, the only roads in cross 2,000 m passes
Expect customs checks leaving into France/Spain: duty-free limits (e.g. 300 cigarettes, 5 L wine) are enforced
Weekend and holiday traffic jams on the CG-2/N-22 corridor to France are notorious in ski season
driving.car_recommended_for: Reaching trailheads (Tristaina, Sorteny), village-hopping Ordino-Canillo, arriving from France
driving.car_not_needed_in: Andorra la Vella and Escaldes (walkable, cheap L1-L6 city buses)

must_see.name: Grandvalira ski area
must_see.why: 210 km of pistes, big-resort skiing at 60-70% of Alpine prices.

must_see.name: Caldea thermal spa
must_see.why: Southern Europe's largest thermal lagoon complex, ideal after ski or trail days (~€35-43 for 3h).

must_see.name: Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley
must_see.why: UNESCO-listed roadless glacial valley, hike or sleep in unstaffed stone refuges for free.

must_see.name: Tristaina lakes
must_see.why: Three turquoise tarns reached in a 2h loop above the Arcalis road; the classic Andorran hike.

must_see.name: Mirador Roc del Quer
must_see.why: A glass-floored skywalk jutting over a 500 m drop, Andorra's best cheap thrill (~€6).

must_see.name: Ordino village
must_see.why: Stone-built old Andorra, a UNESCO biosphere base far from the duty-free bustle.

must_see.name: Sant Joan de Caselles
must_see.why: A perfect 11th-century Romanesque church, one of 40 scattered along the valleys.

must_see.name: Avinguda Meritxell shopping
must_see.why: Duty-free electronics, perfume and tobacco ~20% below EU prices, the reason half of Spain drives up.

insights: Tourist tax ~€1-3 per person/night by hotel category (+4.5% IGI), max 7 nights; a peak-season doubling has been proposed for coming seasons
Andorra is NOT in the EU: EU mobile roaming plans usually exclude it and rates are brutal, download offline maps and use Wi-Fi
No airport, budget the €35-40 bus from Barcelona or Toulouse into your Ryanair trip cost
Prices for meals and lift passes are noticeably below France/Spain, but hotel rates spike in February and around holidays
Pharmacy, sunglasses, electronics and fuel are cheap (duty-free), fill the tank before leaving
Tap water is safe mountain water everywhere
food: Pyrenean grilled meats a la llosa (on slate)
events: Festa Major d'Andorra la Vella (first weekend of August)

Monaco.best_time_note: Spring and early autumn are ideal; late May is Grand Prix chaos (roads closed, prices triple) unless the race itself is the reason you're coming.

rail.note: Monaco Monte-Carlo station has trains every 15-30 min from Nice (~25 min, ~€4-5), basing yourself in Nice and day-tripping is the budget play.

bus.note: The coastal ZOU! bus from Nice costs ~€2.50 and hugs the Corniche; CAM city buses are €2.

driving.tolls: No tolls in Monaco; the French A8 approach is tolled. Parking garages are pricey (though many offer the first hour free).
warnings: Skip the car entirely, the principality is 2 km wide, garages are expensive and GP-season closures (late May) paralyse traffic
French Riviera low-emission rules and dense traffic apply the moment you leave
driving.car_recommended_for: Nothing within Monaco; only useful for touring the Corniche roads and perched villages (Eze, La Turbie) around it
driving.car_not_needed_in: The entire principality, public lifts, escalators and buses cover it

must_see.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo & Casino Square
must_see.why: Belle Epoque icon, the atrium is free to enter; gaming rooms cost ~€19, 18+ with ID and dress code after dark.

must_see.name: Oceanographic Museum
must_see.why: Cousteau's legendary aquarium built into the cliff face, the principality's best-value paid attraction.

must_see.name: Prince's Palace & Le Rocher old town
must_see.why: Watch the changing of the guard at 11:55 sharp, free, then wander the lanes of the Rock.

must_see.name: F1 circuit walk
must_see.why: Walk the actual Grand Prix track, Fairmont hairpin, tunnel and Rascasse, for free, any day of the year.

must_see.name: Port Hercule
must_see.why: Superyacht-spotting central; come during GP or Yacht Show weeks for peak absurdity.

must_see.name: Marche de la Condamine
must_see.why: The locals' food hall, barbagiuan and socca lunch for under €10, the cheapest real meal in Monaco.

must_see.name: Larvotto beach
must_see.why: A free public beach in the world's most expensive country.

must_see.name: Japanese Garden & Princess Grace rose garden
must_see.why: Two immaculate free gardens, Monaco does free surprisingly well.

insights: No tourist tax in Monaco, but hotels start ~€200/night, so nearly everyone sleeps in Nice or Menton and day-trips by train
Monaco is not in the EU but uses the euro; French SIM/roaming works, though phones sometimes latch onto Monaco Telecom, check your plan
Casino: 18+, passport required, entry fee for gaming rooms, smart dress evenings; shorts fine for the free atrium by day
Use the free public lifts and escalators, they save hundreds of stair-steps between the port and Monte-Carlo
A picnic from the Condamine market or Carrefour beats €25 tourist-trap sandwiches on Casino Square
Grand Prix week (late May): grandstand tickets from ~€80 (Fri) but hotels within 30 km sell out months ahead
food: Barbagiuan (fried chard-and-ricotta pastry, the national dish)

San Marino.best_time_note: May-June and September give clear views from Monte Titano without the July-August day-tripper waves rolling up from the Rimini beaches.

rail.note: No trains in San Marino. Take Trenitalia to Rimini, then the direct shuttle bus up the mountain (~50 min).

bus.note: Roughly hourly from Rimini station, ~€6 one-way; last returns are early evening, check before staying for sunset.

driving.tolls: No tolls in San Marino; Italian A14 tolls apply getting there. Fuel is slightly cheaper than in Italy.
warnings: The historic centre atop Monte Titano is closed to non-resident traffic, use numbered car parks (P1-P13) and walk or ride the cable car from Borgo Maggiore
The switchback climb is steep; brakes overheat on the way down in summer
driving.car_recommended_for: Combining with Emilia-Romagna hill towns (San Leo, Urbino) on a road trip
driving.car_not_needed_in: The capital itself, arrive by Rimini bus and everything is on foot

must_see.name: Guaita (First Tower)
must_see.why: The 11th-century fortress on Monte Titano's cliff edge, the walk between the towers is the country's defining experience.

must_see.name: Cesta (Second Tower) & Montale
must_see.why: Cesta holds the medieval-weapons museum; Montale is photogenically off-limits, capping the UNESCO ridgeline.

must_see.name: Piazza della Liberta
must_see.why: Seat of the world's oldest republic (301 AD); catch the summer changing of the Guard ceremony.

must_see.name: Passo delle Streghe
must_see.why: The 'Witches' Path' between Guaita and Cesta, with 750 m drops to Romagna on both sides.

must_see.name: Borgo Maggiore & the funivia
must_see.why: Ride the cable car up the cliff (~€4.50 return) instead of driving, the approach IS the attraction.

must_see.name: Basilica del Santo
must_see.why: Neoclassical shrine of Saint Marinus, the stonecutter who founded the republic.

must_see.name: Museo di Stato
must_see.why: The republic's eccentric national collection, from Etruscan finds to diplomatic gifts.

must_see.name: San Leo (just outside)
must_see.why: A sister crag-top fortress 30 min away, pair the two for one of Italy's least-known great day trips.

insights: No border checks from Italy and no tourist tax; the famous souvenir passport stamp costs €5 at the tourist office
It's a genuine duty-free zone: fuel, perfume, sunglasses and spirits run noticeably cheaper than Italy
Day-trip crowds peak 11:00-16:00; stay one night and you get floodlit ramparts and empty lanes to yourself
Everything is steep cobbles, proper shoes, and expect fog (or magical cloud-inversions) outside summer
Ryanair flies to Rimini seasonally; otherwise Bologna airport + train to Rimini is the standard budget route
Combo ticket for both climbable towers is ~€8 and worth it
food: Sangiovese and Moscato from the Consorzio Vini tipici
events: San Marino & Rimini Riviera MotoGP at nearby Misano (September)

Malta.best_time_note: April-June and September-October combine 20-27C swimming weather with thinner crowds; July-August is 32C+, packed and pricier, while winters are mild but windy.

rail.note: No trains, the whole country runs on buses plus harbour ferries (Valletta-Sliema/Three Cities) and the Gozo Channel ferry from Cirkewwa (pay ~€4.65 on the return leg only).

bus.note: Single tickets ~€2.50 (2h validity); the tallinja app or Explore card is cheaper for multi-day stays, buses get very crowded and can skip stops in summer.

driving.tolls: No tolls anywhere.
warnings: Drive on the LEFT, the biggest hazard for continental visitors, especially at roundabouts
Local driving style is assertive and lane discipline loose; Malta has EU-high accident rates for its size
Valletta has a camera-enforced CVA charge for driving in; park outside and walk or ferry in
Roads to remote coves are narrow, rough and poorly signed
driving.car_recommended_for: Gozo, Dingli Cliffs and the west coast, reaching remote bays (Ghajn Tuffieha, Fomm ir-Rih) on your own clock
driving.car_not_needed_in: Valletta, Sliema-St Julian's corridor, the Three Cities (buses + ferries cover them)

must_see.name: Valletta
must_see.why: A whole baroque capital built by the Knights in 15 years, St John's Co-Cathedral's Caravaggios justify the €15 entry.

must_see.name: Mdina & Rabat
must_see.why: The silent walled former capital, straight off a film set (it literally was King's Landing), go at dusk after tour groups leave.

must_see.name: Hypogeum of Hal Saflieni
must_see.why: A 5,000-year-old underground temple with a strict ~80-visitors/day cap, book weeks ahead on heritagemalta.mt.

must_see.name: Hagar Qim & Mnajdra temples
must_see.why: Megalithic temples older than Stonehenge and the pyramids, on a clifftop above the sea.

must_see.name: Blue Lagoon, Comino
must_see.why: Absurdly turquoise water, take the first boat (or kayak from Gozo) because by 11:00 it's shoulder-to-shoulder.

must_see.name: Gozo: Cittadella & Ramla Bay
must_see.why: Malta's slower sister island: a golden-sand bay, hilltop citadel and salt pans, all doable with a day of buses or a rental.

must_see.name: Marsaxlokk Sunday fish market
must_see.why: Painted luzzu boats and the island's best-value seafood lunches along the quay.

must_see.name: Dingli Cliffs
must_see.why: 250 m sea cliffs with free sunset views, bring a picnic.

must_see.name: Blue Grotto
must_see.why: €10 boat trips into glowing sea caves, best before 10:00 when the light hits the water.

must_see.name: The Three Cities
must_see.why: Vittoriosa's lanes predate Valletta and see a fraction of its visitors, cross by traditional dghajsa water taxi (~€2).

insights: Eco-contribution tripled on 1 Jul 2026: now €1.50 per person/night (18+), capped at €22.50 per stay, collected by your accommodation
Book the Hypogeum weeks ahead (tiny daily cap); Blue Lagoon boats and summer buses to it fill by mid-morning
Tap water is safe but desalinated and tastes poor, most visitors buy 6-packs of bottled water for ~€2 at supermarkets
English is co-official: signage, menus and prices are effortless for anglophones
Jellyfish blooms (mauve stingers) periodically close swimming spots, check the daily flags
Village festa season (June-September) means free fireworks and band marches somewhere every weekend
Cards are widely accepted, but small kiosks, boat skippers and some buses want cash
Ryanair flies Charleroi-Malta year-round, and the island's small size means 3-4 days covers a lot
food: Ftira bread with tuna and capers
Cisk lager and Kinnie bitter-orange soda
events: Isle of MTV free concert, Floriana (June/July)
